XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I set out priorities for healthcare in Wales, including Sir Fynwy Torfaen, in my oral statement on 2 June. Mae'r rhain yn canolbwyntio ar wella mynediad, cryfhau gwasanaethau lleol, darparu mwy o ofal yn nes at y cartref, lleihau amseroedd aros, cefnogi staff a sicrhau cynaliadwyedd hirdymor.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. In order to improve services for all in my constituency and across Wales, we need to ensure that we protect women's rights in line with the Supreme Court ruling that sex means biological sex, therefore protecting single-sex wards, toilets and changing rooms. We all know the case of the Darlington nurses, so this is crucial to prevent these situations not only for patients, but for staff. Language in the NHS is also important. Women and girls menstruate, women breastfeed, men don't. In health, this is important. Sex means biological sex. Facts are important. Let's cut the nonsense. Minister, will you now look into urgently making changes in our Welsh NHS in line with the ruling to protect women and girls in Wales, as they've already begun to do in other parts of the UK?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Er mwyn gwella gwasanaethau i bawb yn fy etholaeth a ledled Cymru, mae angen inni sicrhau ein bod yn diogelu hawliau menywod yn unol â dyfarniad y Goruchaf Lys fod rhyw yn golygu rhyw biolegol, gan ddiogelu wardiau, toiledau ac ystafelloedd newid un rhyw. Mae pob un ohonom yn gyfarwydd ag achos nyrsys Darlington, felly mae hyn yn hanfodol i atal y sefyllfaoedd hyn nid yn unig i gleifion, ond i staff. Mae iaith yn y GIG hefyd yn bwysig. Menywod a merched sy'n cael mislif, menywod sy'n bwydo ar y fron, nid dynion. Ym maes iechyd, mae hyn yn bwysig. Mae rhyw yn golygu rhyw biolegol. Mae ffeithiau'n bwysig. Gadewch inni roi’r gorau i’r nonsens. Weinidog, a wnewch chi edrych nawr ar wneud newidiadau ar frys yn GIG Cymru yn unol â’r dyfarniad i ddiogelu menywod a merched yng Nghymru, fel y maent eisoes wedi dechrau ei wneud mewn rhannau eraill o’r DU?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llywydd, this question has been exercised many times in this Chamber, so I will re-emphasise the fact that this Government will respect the court ruling, of course, but we are clear that we will treat everybody within the NHS—who enters our NHS, who enters our GP surgeries, who enters our hospitals, wherever they are in the health and care system—with the dignity and respect that they deserve, respecting who they are and being there for them in their hour of need.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Lywydd, mae’r cwestiwn hwn wedi’i ofyn sawl gwaith yn y Siambr hon, felly rwyf am ailbwysleisio’r ffaith y bydd y Llywodraeth hon yn parchu dyfarniad y llys wrth gwrs, ond rydym hefyd yn glir y byddwn yn trin pawb o fewn y GIG—sy’n mynd i mewn i’n GIG, sy’n mynd i mewn i’n meddygfeydd, sy’n mynd i mewn i’n hysbytai, lle bynnag y bônt yn y system iechyd a gofal—gyda’r urddas a’r parch y maent yn ei haeddu, gan barchu pwy ydynt a bod yno ar eu cyfer pan fyddant angen hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Cabinet Minister, for that answer. Aneurin Bevan University Health Board is at level 4 escalation for finance, strategy, planning and performance, as well as for urgent and emergency care outcomes. I'm deeply concerned about how this is affecting the most vulnerable patients and those waiting for planned care. Due to longer waits, people are presenting with more complex needs. One person I know of, who has been waiting for a knee replacement, recently fell and broke her hip. I'm very concerned about the long waits that patients in my constituency are facing, and I know that the planned budget, which was voted against last night by Reform and Labour, proposed £145 million to alleviate waiting lists across Wales. What is the Government going to do now to improve the situation for vulnerable patients in Sir Fynwy Torfaen and the wider Aneurin Bevan University Health Board?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich ateb, Weinidog Cabinet. Mae Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Aneurin Bevan ar lefel uwchgyfeirio 4 o ran cyllid, strategaeth, cynllunio a pherfformiad, yn ogystal â chanlyniadau gofal brys a gofal argyfwng. Rwy’n bryderus iawn ynghylch y ffordd y mae hyn yn effeithio ar y cleifion mwyaf agored i niwed a’r rheini sy’n aros am ofal a gynlluniwyd. Oherwydd amseroedd aros hwy, mae pobl yn ymgyflwyno gydag anghenion mwy cymhleth. Fe wnaeth un unigolyn y gwn amdani, sydd wedi bod yn aros am lawdriniaeth i gael pen-glin newydd, syrthio'n ddiweddar a thorri ei chlun. Rwy'n bryderus iawn am yr amseroedd aros hir y mae cleifion yn fy etholaeth yn eu hwynebu, a gwn fod y gyllideb a gynlluniwyd, y pleidleisiodd Reform a Llafur yn ei herbyn neithiwr, wedi cynnig £145 miliwn i fynd i'r afael â rhestrau aros ledled Cymru. Beth y mae'r Llywodraeth yn mynd i'w wneud nawr i wella'r sefyllfa i gleifion agored i niwed yn Sir Fynwy Torfaen a Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Aneurin Bevan yn fwy cyffredinol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for the question from the Member. As the Member said, in the supplementary budget yesterday, as far as health is concerned, we had a focus on outcomes, on improving people's health and well-being by introducing more funding into tackling the waiting lists, and it was extremely disappointing, to say the least, to see people who have said that they wanted to support such a policy vote against it. We want to improve people's outcomes and make sure that the impact on patients is better. So, we have made sure that NHS Wales Performance and Improvement are now involved. They have agreed an intervention approach in the Aneurin Bevan University Health Board to support them. Their improvement plan focuses on supporting frail and older people in the community—exactly answering the points that the Member raised—increasing the front-door capacity for people with complex needs and ensuring timely discharge. We have also allocated an additional £3 million this year to enable the delivery of the improvement plan.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am y cwestiwn gan yr Aelod. Fel y dywedodd yr Aelod, yn y gyllideb atodol ddoe, o ran iechyd, fe wnaethom ganolbwyntio ar ganlyniadau, ar wella iechyd a lles pobl drwy gyflwyno mwy o gyllid i fynd i'r afael â'r rhestrau aros, ac roedd yn siomedig iawn, a dweud y lleiaf, gweld pobl sydd wedi dweud eu bod am gefnogi polisi o'r fath yn pleidleisio yn ei erbyn. Rydym am wella canlyniadau i bobl a sicrhau bod yr effaith ar gleifion yn well. Felly, rydym wedi sicrhau bod Perfformiad a Gwella GIG Cymru bellach yn rhan o'r gwaith. Maent wedi cytuno ar ddull ymyrryd ym Mwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Aneurin Bevan i'w cefnogi. Mae eu cynllun gwella'n canolbwyntio ar gefnogi pobl fregus a hŷn yn y gymuned—i ateb yr union bwyntiau a gododd yr Aelod—gan gynyddu'r capasiti drws blaen ar gyfer pobl ag anghenion cymhleth a sicrhau bod pobl yn cael eu rhyddhau mewn modd amserol. Rydym hefyd wedi dyrannu £3 miliwn yn ychwanegol eleni er mwyn helpu i gyflawni'r cynllun gwella.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Secretary, I have had constituents tell me that, when calling 999, they are no longer being given an estimated arrival time for ambulances. Now, I understand this may reflect operational practice rather than a formal policy, particularly following recent changes to ambulance performance measures. However, not knowing when help is likely to arrive can add significant anxiety for patients and their families—should they wait or should they find another means of getting to hospital? Can you therefore clarify the position on providing ETAs and assure the Senedd that communication and reassurance remain part of the ambulance service approach? And what advice would you give to the public?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ysgrifennydd y Cabinet, mae etholwyr wedi dweud wrthyf, wrth ffonio 999, nad ydynt bellach yn cael amser cyrraedd amcangyfrifedig ar gyfer ambiwlansys. Nawr, rwy'n deall y gallai hyn adlewyrchu arferion gweithredol yn hytrach na pholisi ffurfiol, yn enwedig yn dilyn newidiadau diweddar i fesurau perfformiad ambiwlansys. Fodd bynnag, gall peidio â gwybod pryd y mae cymorth yn debygol o gyrraedd ychwanegu pryder sylweddol i gleifion a'u teuluoedd—a ddylent aros neu a ddylent ddod o hyd i ffordd arall o gyrraedd yr ysbyty? Felly, a allwch chi egluro beth yw'r safbwynt o ran darparu amseroedd cyrraedd amcangyfrifedig a rhoi sicrwydd i'r Senedd fod cyfathrebu a sicrwydd yn parhau i fod yn rhan o ddull gweithredu'r gwasanaeth ambiwlans? A pha gyngor y byddech chi'n ei roi i'r cyhoedd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. The Member will be aware—I'm sure he was a member of the committee when we discussed ambulances in the last Senedd—that why those changes were brought in is because of recommendations put forward by our committee. The Member will have, I'm sure, read the story in the news recently about how other countries are now looking at the introduction of that purple target and how they are improving outcomes in the ambulance trust, which is to be welcomed. However, the broader point I think the Member raises about communication is important. Communication across the board in the NHS has not been where it should be in ensuring that patients know what to expect and when to expect it. So, this is something, certainly, I will be picking up in my regular meetings with the ambulance trust, and I'm more than happy to keep the Member informed on developments on that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Bydd yr Aelod yn ymwybodol—rwy'n siŵr ei fod yn aelod o'r pwyllgor y tro diwethaf inni drafod ambiwlansys yn y Senedd ddiwethaf—mai'r rheswm pam y cyflwynwyd y newidiadau hynny yw oherwydd argymhellion a gyflwynwyd gan ein pwyllgor. Bydd yr Aelod, rwy'n siŵr, wedi darllen y stori yn y newyddion yn ddiweddar ynglŷn â sut y mae gwledydd eraill bellach yn edrych ar gyflwyno'r targed porffor a sut y maent yn gwella canlyniadau yn yr ymddiriedolaeth ambiwlans, sydd i'w groesawu. Fodd bynnag, mae'r pwynt ehangach y credaf fod yr Aelod yn ei godi ynglŷn â chyfathrebu'n bwysig. Nid yw cyfathrebu yn gyffredinol yn y GIG wedi bod cystal ag y dylai fod o ran sicrhau bod cleifion yn gwybod beth i'w ddisgwyl a phryd i'w ddisgwyl. Felly, mae hyn yn rhywbeth y byddaf yn sicr yn ei godi yn fy nghyfarfodydd rheolaidd gyda'r ymddiriedolaeth ambiwlans, ac rwy'n fwy na pharod i roi gwybod i'r Aelod am unrhyw ddatblygiadau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: When patients need access to specialist care outside of their health board area, I expect the commissioning health board to have put in place robust pathway arrangements so that people receive seamless, high-quality care. The nature of these arrangements will depend on the specific condition in question.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Pan fydd cleifion angen mynediad at ofal arbenigol y tu allan i'w hardal bwrdd iechyd, rwy'n disgwyl i'r bwrdd iechyd sy'n comisiynu fod wedi rhoi trefniadau llwybr cadarn ar waith fel bod pobl yn cael gofal di-dor o ansawdd uchel. XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Minister. I have personal experience of this issue. My father was rushed into hospital in Hereford, across the border, 42 miles away from home, after suffering a heart attack whilst, ironically, teaching cardiopulmonary resuscitation. He had then to be transferred to Wolverhampton—and this was actually the hospital that he was born in—where he was eventually given a quadruple heart bypass. The journey there and the length of his stay, and the difficulty in visiting him, all added to the stress of the experience. The whole experience was stressful for him and his loved ones. The scale of the challenge posed by cardiovascular ill health can be judged by the fact that British Heart Foundation Cymru say that there are around 26,000 people living with cardiovascular disease in Gwynedd Maldwyn alone today, and that number is growing. This disease causes 57 deaths each month and 680 deaths each year in my constituency alone. The British Heart Foundation calculate that the total annual healthcare cost of this disease across Wales is £770 million. Whilst the National Adult Cardiac Surgery Audit includes data for waiting times and surgery performed in England and Wales, not all data is available for Wales, which makes it much harder to scrutinise the Wales NHS performance.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Mae gennyf brofiad personol o'r mater hwn. Cafodd fy nhad ei ruthro i'r ysbyty yn Henffordd, dros y ffin, 42 milltir o'i gartref, ar ôl dioddef trawiad ar y galon wrth addysgu adfywio cardiopwlmonaidd, yn eironig ddigon. Yna, bu'n rhaid mynd ag ef i Wolverhampton—sef yr ysbyty lle'i ganed mewn gwirionedd—lle cafodd lawdriniaeth ddargyfeiriol bedwarplyg ar ei galon. Ychwanegodd y daith yno a hyd ei arhosiad, a pha mor anodd oedd mynd i ymweld ag ef, at straen y profiad. Roedd y profiad cyfan yn drallodus iddo ef a'i anwyliaid. Gellir dirnad maint yr her a achosir gan afiechyd cardiofasgwlaidd yn sgil y ffaith bod British Heart Foundation Cymru yn dweud bod oddeutu 26,000 o bobl yn byw gyda chlefyd cardiofasgwlaidd yng Ngwynedd Maldwyn yn unig heddiw, ac mae'r nifer hwnnw ar gynnydd. Mae'r clefyd hwn yn achosi 57 o farwolaethau bob mis a 680 o farwolaethau bob blwyddyn yn fy etholaeth i yn unig. Mae'r British Heart Foundation yn cyfrifo bod cost flynyddol y clefyd i ofal iechyd ledled Cymru yn £770 miliwn i gyd. Er bod yr Archwiliad Cenedlaethol o Lawfeddygaeth y Galon i Oedolion yn cynnwys data ar gyfer amseroedd aros a llawdriniaethau a gyflawnir yng Nghymru a Lloegr, nid yw'r holl ddata ar gael ar gyfer Cymru, sy'n ei gwneud yn llawer anos craffu ar berfformiad GIG Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiwn, plis, Claire.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A question, please, Claire.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Sorry. Can the Minister please tell the Senedd what plans he has to ensure that all relevant data for Wales is made available to us?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae’n ddrwg gennyf. A all y Gweinidog ddweud wrth y Senedd pa gynlluniau sydd ganddo i sicrhau bod yr holl ddata perthnasol ar gyfer Cymru ar gael i ni?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Firstly, can I say how sorry I am to hear of the experiences that you had to go through, and for your father? It must have been distressing and I sincerely hope that your father had a full recovery in that period.

The Member also raises an important point about the long distances involved in accessing such services, an issue that, of course, is especially pronounced in rural areas like Gwynedd Maldwyn. This is why our agenda has a particular emphasis on addressing disproportionate geographic barriers to accessing treatment with actions in the first 100 days plan, as well as longer term measures designed to support this objective.

In terms of the specific issues raised on data, the NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee is responsible for commissioning cardiac surgery on behalf of health boards in Wales. As part of the commissioning requirements, centres in Wales and those commissioned in England must submit data to the National Cardiac Audit Programme, which is funded by the Welsh Government. Now, while the most recent reports from the National Adult Cardiac Surgery Audit appear to contain data from commissioned centres in Wales, and along the border with Wales, that isn't to say that this data provides the entire spectrum of patients' experiences, and continuous reviewing and refining is of course a very important element of data handling. So, I'd be grateful, therefore, if the Member could write to me with further details on the specific gaps that she has found, and I'll instruct my officials to make enquiries on her behalf.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn gyntaf, a gaf i ddweud ei bod yn flin iawn gennyf glywed am y profiadau y bu'n rhaid ichi fynd drwyddynt, a phrofiad eich tad? Rhaid ei fod wedi bod yn brofiad trallodus ac rwy'n mawr obeithio bod eich tad wedi gwella'n llwyr yn y cyfnod hwnnw.

Mae'r Aelod hefyd yn codi pwynt pwysig am y pellteroedd hir sy'n gysylltiedig â chael mynediad at wasanaethau o'r fath, mater sy'n arbennig o amlwg mewn ardaloedd gwledig fel Gwynedd Maldwyn. Dyma pam y mae ein hagenda yn rhoi pwyslais penodol ar fynd i'r afael â rhwystrau daearyddol anghymesur i gael mynediad at driniaeth gyda chamau gweithredu yn y cynllun 100 diwrnod cyntaf, yn ogystal â mesurau mwy hirdymor a gynlluniwyd i gefnogi'r amcan hwn.

O ran y materion penodol a godwyd ar ddata, Cyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru sy'n gyfrifol am gomisiynu llawfeddygaeth y galon ar ran byrddau iechyd yng Nghymru. Fel rhan o'r gofynion comisiynu, rhaid i ganolfannau yng Nghymru a'r rhai a gomisiynwyd yn Lloegr gyflwyno data i'r Archwiliad Cenedlaethol o Lawfeddygaeth y Galon i Oedolion, a ariennir gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Nawr, er bod adroddiadau diweddaraf yr Archwiliad Cenedlaethol o Lawfeddygaeth y Galon i Oedolion yn ôl pob golwg yn cynnwys data o ganolfannau a gomisiynwyd yng Nghymru ac ar hyd y ffin, nid yw hynny'n golygu bod y data hwn yn darparu'r sbectrwm cyfan o brofiadau cleifion, ac mae adolygu a mireinio parhaus yn elfen bwysig iawn o drin data. Felly, buaswn yn ddiolchgar pe gallai'r Aelod ysgrifennu ataf gyda manylion pellach am y bylchau penodol y mae wedi'u canfod, ac fe gyfarwyddaf fy swyddogion i wneud ymholiadau ar ei rhan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Un o'r heriau mwyaf sy'n wynebu bwrdd iechyd Powys yw'r cynnydd sylweddol yng nghostau triniaethau trawsffiniol a godwyd gan NHS England, sydd wedi cyfrannu at fwlch ariannol o tua £7.8 miliwn. Yn ogystal, mae bwrdd iechyd dyffryn Gwy yn ceisio codi premiwm gwledig ychwanegol, sydd erbyn hyn oddeutu £13 miliwn. Mae'r materion hyn wedi rhoi pwysau sylweddol ar gyllid y bwrdd iechyd, ac ni fu cefnogaeth gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol i fynd i'r afael â'r costau ychwanegol hyn. Rwy'n croesawu'r buddsoddiad ychwanegol o £145 miliwn i leihau rhestrau aros ledled Cymru. Felly, a all y Gweinidog Cabinet egluro pa asesiad sydd wedi bod i sicrhau bod y buddsoddiad hwn yn elwa triogolion Powys? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: One of the biggest challenges facing Powys health board is the significant increase in the cost of cross-border treatment levied by NHS England, which has contributed to a financial gap of around £7.8 million. In addition, the Wye valley health board is trying to levy an additional rural premium, which now stands at around £13 million. These issues have placed significant pressure on the finances of the health board, and no support was provided by the previous Government to address these additional costs. I welcome the additional investment of £145 million to reduce waiting lists across Wales. So, can the Cabinet Minister explain what assessment has been made to ensure that this investment benefits the residents of Powys? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch am y cwestiwn. Mae'r Aelod yn gwneud pwynt pwysig ar y dechrau drwy sôn am ba mor bwysig oedd y gyllideb atodol ddoe, yn rhoi £145 miliwn yn y flwyddyn ariannol yma er mwyn mynd i'r afael â rhestrau aros, er mwyn gwella'r isadeiledd a gwella'r ddarpariaeth sydd gennym ni ar gyfer rhestrau aros. Roedd yn siomedig aruthrol gweld Aelodau Llafur a'r Rhyddfrydwyr yn ochri efo Reform er mwyn pleidleisio yn erbyn polisïau ac yn erbyn ariannu a fyddai'n mynd i'r afael ag un o'r materion pwysicaf sydd wedi ein hwynebu ni yn y maes iechyd yma yng Nghymru dros y ddegawd a rhagor ddiwethaf.

Ond, mi fyddwn ni'n parhau efo cynlluniau er mwyn mynd i'r afael â'r rhestrau aros hynny, ac mi fydd y rheini'n uniongyrchol o fudd i bobl Powys. Rydyn ni'n ymwybodol o bobl sydd ar restrau aros am amseroedd rhy hir ym Mhowys. Mi fyddan nhw'n cael budd o hyn. Ond, mi fyddwn ni hefyd yn gwneud yn siŵr fod yna rapid diagnostic centre ar gyfer canser yn cael ei chyflwyno ym Mhowys er mwyn gweld pobl ynghynt, yn lle bod pobl yn mynd i'r ysbytai yna sydd ymhell i ffwrdd pan fyddan nhw'n cyrraedd cam 4 yn eu taith canser, sydd yn mynd i fod lawer yn rhy hwyr i nifer ohonyn nhw. Mi fyddwn ni'n edrych yn gynt arnyn nhw ac yn sicrhau eu bod yn cael diagnosis cynt hefyd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you for that question. The Member made an important point at the outset in talking about the importance of the supplementary budget yesterday, in providing £145 million in this financial year in order to address waiting lists, to improve infrastructure and to improve the provision that we have for waiting lists. It was incredibly disappointing to see Labour and Liberal Members siding with Reform to vote against policies and against funding that would tackle one of the most pressing issues that has faced us in health in Wales over a decade and more.

But, we will continue with our plans to address those waiting lists, and this will directly benefit the people of Powys. We are aware of people who have been on waiting lists for far too long in Powys. They will benefit from this. But, we will also ensure that there is a rapid diagnostic centre for cancer introduced in Powys too so that people are seen earlier, rather than people going to hospitals that are long distances away when they get to stage 4 in their cancer journey, which will be far too late for many of them. We will see them more quickly and ensure that they get an earlier diagnosis too.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. First of all, the Reform UK spokesperson, James Evans.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Can the Cabinet Minister tell us when two-year waits will be eliminated?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. A all y Gweinidog Cabinet ddweud wrthym pryd y bydd amseroedd aros dwy flynedd yn cael eu dileu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We've been very clear that two-year waits will be tackled in a matter of months.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym wedi dweud yn glir iawn y byddwn yn mynd i'r afael ag amseroedd aros dwy flynedd mewn mater o fisoedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's now 'a matter of months'. We've heard 'a matter of weeks'. We've heard the finance secretary say it's going to be 12 months. We've heard you say it could be years. Now, it is going to be months, not weeks. So, can you tell us what month these are going to be eliminated, because the Government in Wales are very good at doing slick social media clips, but they're not very good on the detail, are they? That's the problem at the minute. You say it's going to be months. People waiting in pain across Wales aren't going to be very happy about that. They want to know an absolute timeline of when they're going to be eliminated, when they can expect their letters to come through for operations, and you should be able to provide that detail today.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae bellach yn 'fater o fisoedd'. Rydym wedi clywed 'mater o wythnosau'. Rydym wedi clywed yr ysgrifennydd cyllid yn dweud y bydd yn 12 mis. Rydym wedi eich clywed chi'n dweud y gallai fod yn flynyddoedd. Nawr, mae'n mynd i fod yn fisoedd, nid wythnosau. Felly, a allwch chi ddweud wrthym ym mha fis y byddant yn cael eu dileu, gan fod y Llywodraeth yng Nghymru yn dda iawn am greu clipiau slic ar gyfer y cyfryngau cymdeithasol, ond nid ydynt yn dda iawn ar y manylion. Dyna’r broblem ar y funud. Rydych chi'n dweud y bydd yn cymryd misoedd. Nid yw pobl sy'n aros mewn poen ledled Cymru yn mynd i fod yn hapus iawn ynglŷn â hynny. Maent eisiau amserlen bendant o ran pryd y byddant yn cael eu dileu, pryd y gallant ddisgwyl eu llythyrau ar gyfer llawdriniaethau, a dylech allu darparu'r manylion hynny heddiw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member will be aware that the previous Government set a number of targets and failed to reach them because they weren't realistic. We are absolutely realistic in how we are investing this money into improving outcomes so that people are seen quicker. We know that we've got issues around gynaecology. We know we've got issues around cataracts. We know about orthopaedics. So, these are the things that we need to look at and improve. That's why we're going to set up the elective care hub, so that we can see people quicker, so that people can get their treatment within the time frame that is required, so that they improve and can get on with their lives. So, we're absolutely clear. We've been clear all along. I'm not quite sure where these questions come from. Everything we've said in the past, we are sticking by. We will be achieving this in a matter of months. However, let me remind you that you and your colleagues and others here voted against the budget yesterday, which had £145 million in order to tackle this. So, let's not have any crocodile tears that you are concerned about waiting lists. Clearly, you're not. If you were, you'd have supported the supplementary budget so that we could get this money onto the front line to see people as soon as possible.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Bydd yr Aelod yn ymwybodol fod y Llywodraeth flaenorol wedi gosod nifer o dargedau ac wedi methu eu cyflawni am nad oeddent yn realistig. Rydym yn gwbl realistig ynglŷn â sut rydym yn buddsoddi’r arian hwn i wella canlyniadau fel bod pobl yn cael eu gweld yn gynt. Gwyddom fod gennym broblemau mewn perthynas â gynaecoleg. Gwyddom fod gennym broblemau mewn perthynas â chataractau. Gwyddom am orthopedeg. Felly, dyma’r pethau y mae angen inni edrych arnynt a’u gwella. Dyna pam ein bod yn mynd i sefydlu’r hyb gofal a gynlluniwyd, fel y gallwn weld pobl yn gyflymach, fel y gall pobl gael eu triniaeth o fewn yr amserlen sydd ei hangen, fel eu bod yn gwella ac yn gallu parhau â’u bywydau. Felly, rydym yn gwbl glir. Rydym wedi bod yn glir bob amser. Nid wyf yn siŵr o ble y daw’r cwestiynau hyn. Rydym yn glynu wrth bopeth a ddywedwyd gennym yn y gorffennol. Byddwn yn cyflawni hyn mewn mater o fisoedd. Fodd bynnag, gadewch imi eich atgoffa eich bod chi a’ch cyd-Aelodau ac eraill yma wedi pleidleisio yn erbyn y gyllideb ddoe, a oedd yn cynnwys £145 miliwn i fynd i’r afael â hyn. Felly, gadewch inni beidio â chael unrhyw ddagrau crocodeil eich bod yn poeni am restrau aros. Mae'n amlwg nad ydych. Pe baech, fe fyddech chi wedi cefnogi'r gyllideb atodol fel y gallem ddarparu'r arian hwn i'r rheng flaen i allu gweld pobl cyn gynted â phosibl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I want to see more money in our NHS. You could put more money into the NHS if you listened to us and stopped funding some of your vanity projects like planting trees abroad, like some of the projects that you're doing close to home, wasting Welsh Government money looking at Welsh independence, something the public overwhelmingly did not vote for. That's the money that could go into the NHS. We've also heard about 'small change' for overseas offices. That's money that could go into our NHS. That is the reason why we voted against your supplementary budget, because it's a bad deal for Wales.

You just waffled then in your answer to me, Minister, because you didn't actually say when we were going to have those two-year waits gone. You've said 'months'. You've mentioned elective care hubs. By the time they go through planning, by the time the Welsh Government shuffles paper around their offices, that's going to end up being years. You know how the system works. You sat on committee with me when we discussed these things. They don't come overnight. So, can you now outline a date when two-year waits will be eliminated in Wales, because far too many people have been waiting in pain? You promised people you would sort this out, and it's about time you started to deliver, because your honeymoon period cannot go on forever.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwyf am weld mwy o arian yn ein GIG. Gallech roi mwy o arian i mewn i’r GIG pe baech yn gwrando arnom ac yn rhoi’r gorau i ariannu rhai o’ch prosiectau porthi balchder fel plannu coed dramor, fel rhai o’r prosiectau rydych chi'n eu gwneud yn nes at adref, gwastraffu arian Llywodraeth Cymru wrth edrych ar annibyniaeth i Gymru, rhywbeth na phleidleisiodd y mwyafrif llethol o'r cyhoedd drosto. Dyna'r arian a allai fynd i'r GIG. Rydym wedi clywed hefyd am 'newid mân' ar gyfer ein swyddfeydd tramor. Mae hwnnw'n arian a allai fynd i mewn i'n GIG. Dyna’r rheswm pam y gwnaethom bleidleisio yn erbyn eich cyllideb atodol, am ei bod yn fargen wael i Gymru.

Roeddech chi'n siarad ar eich cyfer yn eich ateb i mi, Weinidog, gan na ddywedoch chi mewn gwirionedd pryd y byddem yn gweld diwedd ar yr amseroedd aros dwy flynedd hynny. Rydych chi wedi dweud 'misoedd'. Rydych wedi sôn am hybiau gofal a gynlluniwyd. Erbyn iddynt fynd drwy'r camau cynllunio, erbyn i Lywodraeth Cymru symud papur o amgylch eu swyddfeydd, mae hynny'n mynd i fod yn flynyddoedd. Rydych chi'n gwybod sut y mae'r system yn gweithio. Roeddech chi ar y pwyllgor gyda mi pan oeddem yn trafod y pethau hyn. Nid ydynt yn digwydd dros nos. Felly, a allwch chi amlinellu dyddiad i ni ar gyfer dileu amseroedd aros dwy flynedd yng Nghymru, gan fod gormod lawer o bobl wedi bod yn aros mewn poen? Fe wnaethoch chi addo i bobl y byddech yn datrys hyn, ac mae’n hen bryd ichi ddechrau gwneud hynny, gan na all eich mis mêl bara am byth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You voted against the £145 million yesterday, right? Let me remind you of what your spokesperson, Cai Parry-Jones, said. He set out a number of red lines and, within one of those red lines, why you were opposing it, was the fact that we are employing Indian doctors here. So, clearly, you're not concerned—[Interruption.] Indian nurses, sorry, just to correct the record—Indian nurses. So, let's be clear. You're not concerned about improving the health outcomes of people in Wales. You don't want to see an improved workforce here, which is what we're looking to get to grips with.

Now, you mentioned also planning. It's not all about planning. We've got—and I've mentioned this so many times—a number of under-utilised spaces here, theatre spaces that are not used properly. So, we're going to improve those theatre spaces so that we do see those treatments being carried out and people seen quicker. You should know this as an opposition spokesperson who's been on the committees. It's not difficult; this is what it's about. And we know what we're doing because everything we've put forward is clinically led. Now, if you don't want to see improved outcomes for people, fine, carry on as you are. But we know that we're being led by doctors, by surgeons, by operational managers who've done this successfully in parts of Wales and in England, who will advise us on the best way forward so that we can improve outcomes in Wales. That's our focus.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe wnaethoch chi bleidleisio yn erbyn y £145 miliwn ddoe, oni wnaethoch? Gadewch imi eich atgoffa o’r hyn a ddywedodd eich llefarydd, Cai Parry-Jones. Nododd nifer o linellau coch, ac o fewn un o'r llinellau coch hynny, pam eich bod yn ei gwrthwynebu, oedd y ffaith ein bod yn cyflogi meddygon Indiaidd yma. Felly, yn amlwg, nid ydych chi'n pryderu—[Torri ar draws.] Nyrsys Indiaidd, mae'n ddrwg gennyf, os caf gywiro'r cofnod—nyrsys Indiaidd. Felly, gadewch inni fod yn glir. Nid ydych yn poeni am wella canlyniadau iechyd pobl yng Nghymru. Nid ydych am weld gweithlu gwell yma, a dyna rydym ni'n bwriadu mynd i'r afael ag ef.

Nawr, fe sonioch chi hefyd am gynllunio. Nid cynllunio yw popeth. Mae gennym—ac rwyf wedi sôn am hyn gymaint o weithiau—nifer o ofodau nad ydynt yn cael eu defnyddio'n ddigonol yma, gofodau theatr nad ydynt yn cael eu defnyddio'n briodol. Felly, rydym yn mynd i wella'r mannau theatr hynny fel bod triniaethau'n cael eu cynnal a phobl yn cael eu gweld yn gynt. Dylech wybod hyn fel llefarydd yr wrthblaid sydd wedi bod yn aelod o'r pwyllgorau. Nid yw'n anodd; dyma hanfod y mater. Ac rydym yn gwybod beth a wnawn am fod popeth a gynigiwyd gennym wedi'i arwain yn glinigol. Nawr, os nad ydych chi eisiau gweld canlyniadau gwell i bobl, iawn, daliwch ati. Ond fe wyddom ni ein bod yn cael ein harwain gan feddygon, gan lawfeddygon, gan reolwyr gweithredol sydd wedi gwneud hyn yn llwyddiannus mewn rhannau o Gymru ac yn Lloegr, a fydd yn ein cynghori ar y ffordd orau ymlaen er mwyn inni allu gwella canlyniadau yng Nghymru. Dyna yw ein ffocws.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Jayne Bryant.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Jayne Bryant.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Our dedicated staff in our NHS work tirelessly, and in recent weeks many have experienced incredibly challenging working conditions due to the hot weather. Last month, the Welsh Ambulance Services University NHS Trust declared a critical incident following one of the busiest periods of sustained pressure on services in recent years. Demand was well in excess of normal levels as a result of the extreme heat, and I understand there was a noticeable increase in the number of young people presenting with symptoms of dehydration. We're accustomed to the NHS needing to prepare for the winter pressures, but what action is the Government taking to ensure that services, buildings and the workforce are equipped to deal with the impact of hot weather?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Mae staff ymroddedig ein GIG yn gweithio'n ddiflino, ac yn yr wythnosau diwethaf, mae llawer wedi wynebu amodau gwaith heriol iawn oherwydd y tywydd poeth. Y mis diwethaf, cyhoeddodd Ymddiriedolaeth Brifysgol GIG Gwasanaethau Ambiwlans Cymru ddigwyddiad critigol yn dilyn un o'r cyfnodau prysuraf o bwysau parhaus ar wasanaethau yn y blynyddoedd diwethaf. Roedd y galw ymhell uwchlaw'r lefelau arferol o ganlyniad i'r gwres eithafol, ac rwy'n deall bod cynnydd amlwg wedi bod yn nifer y bobl ifanc a oedd yn ymgyflwyno â symptomau dadhydradiad. Rydym wedi arfer â'r angen i'r GIG baratoi ar gyfer pwysau'r gaeaf, ond pa gamau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i sicrhau bod gwasanaethau, adeiladau a'r gweithlu yn cael adnoddau addas i ymdopi ag effaith tywydd poeth?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you to the Member for that question and raising the issue. First of all, I think we need to recognise and be realistic that this is happening. Global warming is happening in front of our eyes. We're experiencing it. Some people want to deny that. Again, I'm pointing my finger at Reform, who are more than happy to say it's not happening. This is man-made, and it's impacting on the well-being of people in Wales, the people that you represent, and it's incumbent on us to respond to this as soon as we can.

The Wales ambulance trust was under significant pressure last week and the week before, and we've seen them step up as well and making sure that they are responding the best they can. I take my hat off to the paramedics, ambulance drivers and the people in that service who've done such terrific work in responding to the various calls that they've received over the last few weeks.

The recent heatwave saw unprecedented demand on the services, resulting in a critical incident being declared and substantial increases in both emergency calls and high acuity incidents. So, we put out a guidance note to all the hospitals and the health boards following the previous heatwave, making sure that they were aware that they needed to prepare for this summer and for the ones coming up.

You will have heard also in my winter pressure statements that I referred to the heatwaves, and the fact that we are now taking the approach of an all-year-round assessment of the situation. We are already preparing bilaterals with various Cabinet Ministers, in this instance the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning, looking at how we need to include those considerations of global warming and the environment around the health system when it comes to planning into those briefings and portfolios, so that we prepare, moving forward, for this in the future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch i'r Aelod am ei chwestiwn ac am godi'r mater. Yn gyntaf oll, credaf fod angen inni gydnabod a bod yn realistig fod hyn yn digwydd. Mae cynhesu byd-eang yn digwydd o flaen ein llygaid. Rydym yn ei brofi. Mae rhai pobl eisiau gwadu hynny. Unwaith eto, rwy'n pwyntio fy mys at Reform, sy'n fwy na pharod i ddweud nad yw'n digwydd. Gwaith dyn yw hyn, ac mae'n effeithio ar lesiant pobl yng Nghymru, y bobl rydych chi'n eu cynrychioli, ac mae'n ddyletswydd arnom i ymateb i hyn cyn gynted ag y gallwn.

Roedd ymddiriedolaeth gwasanaethau ambiwlans Cymru o dan bwysau sylweddol yr wythnos diwethaf a'r wythnos cynt, ac rydym wedi eu gweld yn mynd i'r afael â hyn ac yn sicrhau eu bod yn ymateb cystal ag y gallant. Rwy'n codi fy het i'r parafeddygon, y gyrwyr ambiwlansys a'r bobl yn y gwasanaeth hwnnw sydd wedi gwneud gwaith mor wych yn ymateb i'r galwadau amrywiol y maent wedi'u derbyn dros yr ychydig wythnosau diwethaf.

Achosodd y don wres yn ddiweddar alw digynsail ar y gwasanaethau, gan arwain at ddatgan digwyddiad critigol a chynnydd sylweddol mewn galwadau brys a digwyddiadau aciwtedd uchel. Felly, fe wnaethom gyhoeddi nodyn cyfarwyddyd i'r holl ysbytai a'r byrddau iechyd yn dilyn y don wres flaenorol, gan sicrhau eu bod yn ymwybodol fod angen iddynt baratoi ar gyfer yr haf hwn a'r rhai sydd i ddod.

Byddwch wedi fy nghlywed hefyd yn fy natganiadau ar bwysau'r gaeaf yn cyfeirio at y tonnau gwres, a'r ffaith ein bod bellach yn mabwysiadu dull o asesu'r sefyllfa drwy gydol y flwyddyn. Rydym eisoes yn paratoi trafodaethau dwyochrog gyda gwahanol Weinidogion Cabinet, yn yr achos hwn y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio, gan edrych ar sut y mae angen inni gynnwys ystyriaethau'n ymwneud â chynhesu byd-eang a'r amgylchedd o amgylch y system iechyd o ran cynllunio yn y briffiau a'r portffolios hynny, fel ein bod yn paratoi ar gyfer hyn yn y dyfodol wrth symud ymlaen.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch and, absolutely, the workforce is absolutely crucial. Earlier today, alongside my colleague Shav Taj, I met student midwives from the September 2023 cohort. They feel as though they've been left in limbo, with no jobs available. One newly-qualified midwife told me she was now working as a water technician, and others are working as baristas and in the hospitality sector. The students have been told that there might be opportunities to work in health and social care, but this is not what they want or that they're qualified to do. Now, I know the Minister is aware of the situation, but the student midwives cannot have been clearer today; they feel left behind and they feel without hope.

Welsh Labour protected the NHS Wales bursary scheme, supporting the next generation of healthcare workers to train and work in the Welsh NHS, but, without clinical experience, student midwives can't get jobs and they can't use their degree for anything else. One option would be to extend the bursary for another year to cover the preceptorship training that enables midwives to transition to professional practice. So, will the Welsh Government consider this as one option?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, ac yn sicr, mae'r gweithlu'n gwbl allweddol. Yn gynharach heddiw, gyda fy nghyd-Aelod Shav Taj, cyfarfûm â myfyrwyr bydwreigiaeth o garfan mis Medi 2023. Maent yn teimlo fel pe baent wedi cael eu gadael mewn limbo, heb unrhyw swyddi ar gael. Dywedodd un fydwraig newydd gymhwyso wrthyf ei bod bellach yn gweithio fel technegydd dŵr, ac mae eraill yn gweithio fel baristas ac yn y sector lletygarwch. Dywedwyd wrth y myfyrwyr y gallai fod cyfleoedd i weithio ym maes iechyd a gofal cymdeithasol, ond nid dyma maent eisiau ei wneud na'r hyn y maent yn gymwys i'w wneud. Nawr, gwn fod y Gweinidog yn ymwybodol o'r sefyllfa, ond ni allai'r myfyrwyr bydwreigiaeth fod wedi bod yn gliriach heddiw; maent yn teimlo eu bod wedi'u gadael ar ôl ac maent yn teimlo'n ddiobaith.

Diogelodd Llafur Cymru gynllun bwrsariaeth GIG Cymru, gan gefnogi'r genhedlaeth nesaf o weithwyr gofal iechyd i hyfforddi a gweithio yn GIG Cymru, ond heb brofiad clinigol, ni all myfyrwyr bydwreigiaeth gael swyddi ac ni allant ddefnyddio eu gradd ar gyfer unrhyw beth arall. Un opsiwn fyddai ymestyn y fwrsariaeth am flwyddyn arall i dalu am yr hyfforddiant tiwtoriaeth sy'n galluogi bydwragedd i bontio i ymarfer proffesiynol. Felly, a fydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn ystyried hyn fel un opsiwn?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
So, the issue with the graduates lies squarely on the shoulders of the previous Government. This is an issue that was under your watch, back in 2023. As you said, these students were the cohort going through from 2022-23, and it will take a few years to work through the system. That's why one of the first things that I did when I came into this post was set up a graduate summit, in order to try and find options for as many of these young people as possible. Because here in Wales, different from England, they are streamlined, so a promise is made to them. So we need to try and honour that promise, and it's disappointing that we were left in a position where those promises were broken by the previous Government. So now we're trying to find a long-term solution for this. That's why we've asked Healthcare Inspectorate Wales to work with the health boards, to work with the representative bodies, to bring that plan together, and I expect to see a plan by the end of December—or early autumn, in fact.

Now, when it comes to the bursary scheme, once again, may I just remind you that this wasn't part of any negotiations that you brought forward or discussions that you brought forward for the supplementary budget, which you voted against as a party, in order to improve health outcomes in Wales. I am absolutely more than happy to discuss any options that you might have and consider their impact and assess how they might be included, but I just remind you that, as we have been informed by the Cabinet Minister for Finance, there are massive in-year pressures currently in the health service, and those pressures are only going to get worse as time goes on because of settlements coming down from London and the fact that we don't have a fair funding formula for Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Felly, y Llywodraeth flaenorol sydd ar fai am y broblem gyda'r graddedigion. Mae hon yn broblem a oedd o dan eich goruchwyliaeth chi, yn ôl yn 2023. Fel y dywedoch chi, y myfyrwyr hyn oedd carfan 2022-23, a bydd yn cymryd ychydig flynyddoedd i weithio drwy'r system. Dyna pam mai un o'r pethau cyntaf a wneuthum pan ddeuthum i'r swydd hon oedd sefydlu uwchgynhadledd graddedigion, er mwyn ceisio dod o hyd i opsiynau i gynifer o'r bobl ifanc hyn â phosibl. Oherwydd yma yng Nghymru, yn wahanol i Loegr, mae wedi ei symleiddio, felly mae addewid yn cael ei wneud iddynt. Felly mae angen inni geisio anrhydeddu'r addewid hwnnw, ac mae'n siomedig ein bod wedi cael ein gadael mewn sefyllfa lle torrwyd yr addewidion hynny gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol. Felly rydym nawr yn ceisio dod o hyd i ateb hirdymor ar gyfer hyn. Dyna pam ein bod wedi gofyn i Arolygiaeth Gofal Iechyd Cymru weithio gyda'r byrddau iechyd, i weithio gyda'r cyrff cynrychiadol, i ddod â'r cynllun hwnnw at ei gilydd, ac rwy'n disgwyl gweld cynllun erbyn diwedd mis Rhagfyr—neu ddechrau'r hydref, mewn gwirionedd.

Nawr, o ran y cynllun bwrsariaeth, unwaith eto, a gaf i eich atgoffa nad oedd hyn yn rhan o unrhyw drafodaethau a gyflwynwyd gennych ar gyfer y gyllideb atodol, y pleidleisioch chi yn ei herbyn fel plaid, er mwyn gwella canlyniadau iechyd yng Nghymru. Rwy'n fwy na pharod i drafod unrhyw opsiynau a allai fod gennych ac ystyried eu heffaith ac asesu sut y gellid eu cynnwys, ond rwy'n eich atgoffa, fel y cawsom wybod gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyllid, fod pwysau enfawr yn y flwyddyn ar hyn o bryd yn y gwasanaeth iechyd, a dim ond gwaethygu a wnaiff y pwysau hwnnw wrth i amser fynd heibio oherwydd setliadau sy'n dod o Lundain a'r ffaith nad oes gennym fformiwla gyllido deg i Gymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you so much, Presiding Officer. Cabinet Minister, pancreatic is one of the deadliest cancers in the UK, affecting more than 500 people in Wales every single year. Eight in 10 people are diagnosed at a late stage, when it is often too late for treatment, and 50 per cent of people die within three months of diagnosis. In my own constituency, the one-year survival rate is 23 per cent alone. These shocking figures have been underpinned by a series of late diagnoses and ineffective treatment options, which has meant that only 25 per cent of those with pancreatic cancer will be treated within the Welsh Government's 62-day target.

Vague symptoms make pancreatic cancer incredibly difficult to detect, and 90 per cent of patients visit their GP multiple times before diagnosis. This is because there is currently no early detection test available. However, there is hope on the horizon, with the world's first breath test for pancreatic cancer being developed. This test is currently being trialled across the UK, including in Betsi Cadwaladr, Swansea and Cardiff, and the data so far is really promising. While this development could be game changing, there is still more that could and should be done by the Welsh Government.

Health boards across Wales must be provided with the funding and support that they need to deliver the national optimal pathway for pancreatic cancer, ensuring that everyone diagnosed receives the timely, high-quality care that they truly deserve. So, Cabinet Minister, I know you love to use those words ‘clinically led’. The evidence is right there. What plans does the Welsh Government have to improve care for those diagnosed with pancreatic cancer here in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Lywydd. Weinidog Cabinet, mae canser y pancreas yn un o'r mathau mwyaf angheuol o ganser yn y DU, ac yn effeithio ar fwy na 500 o bobl yng Nghymru bob blwyddyn. Mae wyth o bob deg o bobl yn cael diagnosis ar gam hwyr, pan fo'n aml yn rhy hwyr i gael triniaeth, ac mae 50 y cant o bobl yn marw o fewn tri mis i'r diagnosis. Yn fy etholaeth i, 23 y cant yn unig yw'r gyfradd sy'n goroesi am un flwyddyn. Mae'r ffigurau brawychus hyn wedi'u hategu gan gyfres o ddiagnosisau hwyr ac opsiynau triniaeth aneffeithiol, sydd wedi golygu mai dim ond 25 y cant o'r rheini â chanser y pancreas fydd yn cael eu trin o fewn targed 62 diwrnod Llywodraeth Cymru.

Mae symptomau amhendant yn gwneud canser y pancreas yn anhygoel o anodd ei ganfod, ac mae 90 y cant o gleifion yn ymweld â'u meddyg teulu sawl gwaith cyn cael diagnosis. Y rheswm am hyn yw nad oes prawf canfod cynnar ar gael ar hyn o bryd. Fodd bynnag, mae gobaith ar y gorwel, gyda phrawf anadl cyntaf y byd ar gyfer canser y pancreas yn cael ei ddatblygu. Mae'r prawf hwn yn cael ei dreialu ledled y DU ar hyn o bryd, gan gynnwys ym myrddau Betsi Cadwaladr, Abertawe a Chaerdydd, ac mae'r data'n addawol iawn hyd yma. Er y gallai'r datblygiad hwn newid y dirwedd yn gyfan gwbl, mae mwy y gallai ac y dylai Llywodraeth Cymru ei wneud o hyd.

Mae'n rhaid darparu'r cyllid a'r cymorth sydd ei angen ar fyrddau iechyd ledled Cymru i ddarparu'r llwybr cenedlaethol gorau posibl ar gyfer canser y pancreas, gan sicrhau bod pawb sy'n cael diagnosis yn cael y gofal amserol o ansawdd uchel y maent yn ei haeddu. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, gwn eich bod wrth eich bodd yn defnyddio'r geiriau 'o dan arweiniad clinigol'. Mae'r dystiolaeth yno. Pa gynlluniau sydd gan Lywodraeth Cymru i wella gofal i'r rhai sy'n cael diagnosis o ganser y pancreas yma yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The Member is quite right that the targets reached when it comes to pancreatic cancer—in fact, most of the cancers, especially the rarest cancers in Wales—are not where they should be. As a country, we are seeing far too many people suffer from cancer and losing their lives too early, so we need to get to grips with this.

When you talk about the development with the breath test that you mentioned, which has been trialled, these developments—. There are a lot of things going on in the cancer space at the moment, and it's really exciting to see those developments happening here in Wales. They're not recognised enough. That's why I had conversations and meetings recently with our research and innovation departments within the Welsh NHS to see what more we can do, because we need to attract more clinical trials in Wales, and we need to attract more research here in Wales. So, we're working on that now so that Wales can become a world leader in that and then improve that optimal pathway, which we need to look at. And that will be a specific look in our cancer strategy. You'll have read the cancer strategy written statement that I issued today. Now, that has been welcomed by the Wales Cancer Alliance and we will be working with them and others in order to make sure that that cancer strategy is all-encompassing, is comprehensive and will answer those needs.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Aelod yn llygad ei lle fod y targedau a gyrhaeddir o ran canser y pancreas—y rhan fwyaf o'r canserau mewn gwirionedd, yn enwedig y canserau mwyaf prin yng Nghymru—lle dylent fod. Fel gwlad, rydym yn gweld gormod o bobl yn dioddef o ganser ac yn colli eu bywydau'n rhy gynnar, felly mae angen inni fynd i'r afael â hyn.

Pan fyddwch yn sôn am y datblygiadau gyda'r prawf anadl a grybwyllwyd gennych, sydd wedi'i dreialu, y datblygiadau hyn—. Mae llawer o bethau'n mynd rhagddynt ym maes canser ar hyn o bryd, ac mae'n gyffrous iawn gweld y datblygiadau hynny'n digwydd yma yng Nghymru. Nid ydynt yn cael digon o gydnabyddiaeth. Dyna pam y cefais sgyrsiau a chyfarfodydd yn ddiweddar gyda'n hadrannau ymchwil ac arloesi o fewn GIG Cymru i weld beth arall y gallwn ei wneud, gan fod angen inni ddenu mwy o dreialon clinigol yng Nghymru, ac mae angen inni ddenu mwy o ymchwil yma yng Nghymru. Felly, rydym yn gweithio ar hynny nawr fel y gall Cymru ddod yn arweinydd byd-eang yn hynny o beth ac yna gwella'r llwybr optimaidd y mae angen inni edrych arno. A bydd hynny'n elfen benodol yn ein strategaeth canser. Byddwch wedi darllen y datganiad ysgrifenedig ar y strategaeth canser a gyhoeddais heddiw. Nawr, mae hwnnw wedi'i groesawu gan Gynghrair Canser Cymru, a byddwn yn gweithio gyda nhw ac eraill er mwyn sicrhau bod y strategaeth canser honno'n bellgyrhaeddol, yn gynhwysfawr ac yn ateb yr anghenion hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thanks for your response, Cabinet Minister. You clearly read my mind, because I am sticking with the theme of cancer and I did read the plan in depth and detail. So, Cabinet Minister, as we all know, pancreatic is one of the six less survivable cancers with lung, liver, brain, stomach and oes—. Oesophageal; I do apologise. These six less survivable cancers account for over 40 per cent of all cancer deaths, and people diagnosed with these cancers have a shockingly low life expectancy rate. The average one-year survival rate for a patient diagnosed with a less survivable cancer in Wales is just 39 per cent. This contrasts sharpy with the overall one-year survival rate for all cancers, which is just 70 per cent. Despite this, these cancers receive disproportionately low levels of research funding, contributing to a cycle of poor survival rates and limited treatment advances. The previous Government's pan-cancer approach did not adequately address the deep disparities faced by those diagnosed with less survivable cancers. Only 28 per cent of people with less survivable cancers are diagnosed at stage 1 or 2, compared with 52 per cent for all other cancers. This overwhelmingly late-stage diagnosis limits the potential for treatments that could significantly improve survival rates. Equity in cancer care means ensuring that all patients, regardless of their diagnosis, have an equal opportunity to survive.

Given the challenges for detection and treatment that are specific to these cancers, will the Cabinet Minister commit to including a chapter, or action plan at least, dedicated to less survivable cancers in the new cancer plan here in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am eich ymateb, Weinidog Cabinet. Mae'n amlwg eich bod wedi darllen fy meddwl, gan fy mod yn glynu wrth thema canser ac fe ddarllenais y cynllun yn fanwl ac yn drylwyr. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, fel y gŵyr pob un ohonom, mae'r pancreas yn un o'r chwe chanser llai goroesadwy gyda chanser yr ysgyfaint, yr afu, yr ymennydd, y stumog a'r oesoffagws. Y chwe chanser llai goroesadwy hyn sydd i gyfrif am dros 40 y cant o'r holl farwolaethau canser, ac mae gan bobl sy'n cael diagnosis o'r canserau hyn ddisgwyliad oes syfrdanol o isel. Dim ond 39 y cant yw'r gyfradd oroesi un flwyddyn gyfartalog ar gyfer claf sy'n cael diagnosis o ganser llai goroesadwy yng Nghymru. Mae hyn yn cyferbynnu'n llwyr â'r gyfradd oroesi un flwyddyn gyffredinol ar gyfer pob canser, sef 70 y cant yn unig. Er hyn, mae'r canserau hyn yn cael lefelau anghymesur o isel o gyllid ymchwil, gan gyfrannu at gylch dieflig o gyfraddau goroesi gwael a datblygiadau cyfyngedig o ran triniaeth. Ni wnaeth dull gweithredu pan-ganser y Llywodraeth flaenorol fynd i'r afael yn ddigonol â'r anghydraddoldebau dwfn a wynebir gan y rhai sy'n cael diagnosis o ganserau llai goroesadwy. Dim ond 28 y cant o bobl â chanserau llai goroesadwy sy'n cael diagnosis yng ngham 1 neu 2, o gymharu â 52 y cant ar gyfer pob math arall o ganser. Mae'r diagnosis hwyr hwn, sy'n digwydd ar gam hwyr mewn cymaint o achosion, yn cyfyngu ar botensial triniaethau a allai wella cyfraddau goroesi'n sylweddol. Mae tegwch mewn gofal canser yn golygu sicrhau bod gan bob claf, beth bynnag y bo'u diagnosis, gyfle cyfartal i oroesi.

O ystyried yr heriau sy'n benodol i'r canserau hyn o ran canfod a thriniaeth, a wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet ymrwymo i gynnwys pennod, neu gynllun gweithredu o leiaf, yn benodol ar ganserau llai goroesadwy yn y cynllun canser newydd yma yng Nghymru?
