XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I set out my priorities for NHS Wales on 2 June. This included reducing waiting times and improving access to services. To support this, I've set up an expert panel on the development of surgical hubs and am commissioning an independent review of performance. We have allocated an additional £145 million to support improvements.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Nodais fy mlaenoriaethau ar gyfer GIG Cymru ar 2 Mehefin. Roedd hyn yn cynnwys lleihau amseroedd aros a gwella mynediad at wasanaethau. I gefnogi hyn, rwyf wedi sefydlu panel arbenigol ar ddatblygu hybiau llawfeddygol ac rwy'n comisiynu adolygiad annibynnol o berfformiad. Rydym wedi dyrannu £145 miliwn ychwanegol i gefnogi gwelliannau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Minister. I've been really supportive of the exciting plans for the Llantrisant Health Park, a cross-health-board initiative developed and funded under the last Welsh Labour Government, with over £200 million invested to date. This surgical hub will expand capacity, reduce waiting times and improve patient experience across south-east Wales, including for my constituents in Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr. The first phase of the scheme, which is expected to be delivered next year, will see the creation of that state-of-the-art community diagnostic hub, followed later by orthopaedic surgeries. Improving access to diagnostic and orthopaedic services through investment and collaboration was a priority for the last Welsh Labour Government, so I'd like to ask if these are priorities for you too.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Rwyf wedi bod yn gefnogol iawn i'r cynlluniau cyffrous ar gyfer Parc Iechyd Llantrisant, menter ar draws byrddau iechyd a ddatblygwyd ac a ariannwyd o dan Lywodraeth Lafur ddiwethaf Cymru, gyda dros £200 miliwn wedi'i fuddsoddi hyd yn hyn. Bydd yr hyb llawfeddygol yn ehangu capasiti, yn lleihau amseroedd aros ac yn gwella profiad cleifion ledled de-ddwyrain Cymru, gan gynnwys fy etholwyr ym Mhontypridd Cynon Merthyr. Yng ngham cyntaf y cynllun, y disgwylir iddo gael ei gyflawni y flwyddyn nesaf, bydd yr hyb diagnostig cymunedol o'r radd flaenaf hwnnw'n cael ei greu, gyda llawdriniaethau orthopedig i ddilyn yn nes ymlaen. Roedd gwella mynediad at wasanaethau diagnostig ac orthopedig drwy fuddsoddiad a chydweithio yn flaenoriaeth i Lywodraeth Lafur ddiwethaf Cymru, felly hoffwn ofyn a yw'r rhain yn flaenoriaethau i chithau hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It might well have been a priority for the last Government. I doubt whether it's a priority for your party right now because you voted against the supplementary budget, which offered £145 million to develop diagnostic hubs and elective care hubs across Wales. But, yes, it is a priority.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n ddigon posibl fod hynny'n flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth ddiwethaf. Rwy'n amau a yw'n flaenoriaeth i'ch plaid chi ar hyn o bryd gan ichi bleidleisio yn erbyn y gyllideb atodol, a oedd yn cynnig £145 miliwn i ddatblygu hybiau diagnostig a hybiau gofal a gynlluniwyd ledled Cymru. Ond ydy, mae'n flaenoriaeth.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Minister, patients in Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr continue to face unacceptable long waits for diagnostic tests and orthopaedic treatment. Can the Cabinet Minister outline the specific actions and investment the Welsh Government is providing to support Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board in reducing waiting times? And when can patients expect to see measurable improvements in access to care?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog Cabinet, mae cleifion ym Mhontypridd Cynon Merthyr yn parhau i wynebu amseroedd aros annerbyniol o hir am brofion diagnostig a thriniaethau orthopedig. A all y Gweinidog Cabinet amlinellu'r camau gweithredu a'r buddsoddiad penodol y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu darparu i gefnogi Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg i leihau amseroedd aros? A phryd y gall cleifion ddisgwyl gweld gwelliannau mesuradwy o ran mynediad at ofal?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that. As was mentioned in the previous question, we are looking forward to the development of the Llantrisant Health Park, which will improve outcomes for the people in your area.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Fel y soniwyd yn y cwestiwn blaenorol, rydym yn edrych ymlaen at ddatblygiad Parc Iechyd Llantrisant, a fydd yn gwella canlyniadau i'r bobl yn eich ardal.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Swyddi Gwag yn y Gwasanaeth Iechyd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Health Service Vacancies

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet ddatganiad ar gynllunio ar gyfer swyddi gwag yn y gwasanaeth iechyd? OQ64368
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. Will the Cabinet Minister make a statement on vacancy planning in the health service? OQ64368

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Identifying and planning for future workforce gaps is a core part of effective workforce planning. We're working with health boards, trusts and Health Education and Improvement Wales to strengthen forecasting, enhance workforce intelligence and better align education, training, recruitment and funded posts. This will support safe services now and a sustainable NHS workforce for the future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae nodi a chynllunio ar gyfer bylchau yn y gweithlu yn y dyfodol yn rhan hanfodol o gynllunio'r gweithlu'n effeithiol. Rydym yn gweithio gyda byrddau iechyd, ymddiriedolaethau ac Addysg a Gwella Iechyd Cymru i gryfhau rhagolygon, gwella deallusrwydd y gweithlu ac alinio addysg, hyfforddiant, recriwtio a swyddi a ariennir yn well. Bydd hyn yn cefnogi gwasanaethau diogel nawr a gweithlu GIG cynaliadwy ar gyfer y dyfodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I only wish that was true. There are no NHS jobs for three in 10 nurses graduating in Wales this summer. No-one has told me the wards have too many nurses; many have told me that the wards they have been treated on or visited patients needed more nurses. Student nurses have said they've felt let down, worried and angry after years of unpaid work in the NHS during training and taking out large loans to qualify. Will the health Minister provide, as requested by the Royal College of Nursing, a jobs guarantee for nursing graduates? And you'll want to know where the money is coming from: there's £247 million unallocated, and we only wanted £100 million of that for additional learning needs.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: O, na bai hynny'n wir. Nid oes swyddi GIG i dri o bob 10 nyrs sy'n graddio yng Nghymru yr haf hwn. Nid oes unrhyw un wedi dweud wrthyf fod gan y wardiau ormod o nyrsys; mae llawer wedi dweud wrthyf fod angen mwy o nyrsys ar y wardiau y maent wedi cael eu trin arnynt neu lle maent wedi ymweld â chleifion. Mae myfyrwyr nyrsio wedi dweud eu bod wedi teimlo'n siomedig, yn bryderus ac yn flin ar ôl blynyddoedd o waith di-dâl yn y GIG yn ystod eu hyfforddiant ac ar ôl benthyg llawer o arian i gymhwyso. A wnaiff y Gweinidog iechyd ddarparu warant swyddi i raddedigion nyrsio, fel y gofynnodd y Coleg Nyrsio Brenhinol amdani? A byddwch eisiau gwybod o ble mae'r arian yn dod: mae £247 miliwn heb ei ddyrannu, a dim ond £100 miliwn ohono roeddem ei eisiau ar gyfer anghenion dysgu ychwanegol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member will be aware that—[Interruption.] The Member will be aware that we have a streamlining process in Wales, which is meant to ensure that they have jobs, that nurses and midwives and others have jobs when they finish their graduation. Unfortunately, because of the previous Government's failure to honour this, many nurses, midwives and paramedics in Wales today can't find those jobs, that's why we set up the graduate summit. So, I won't exercise that answer again; I've answered it once already, so forgive me if I don't go any further down that line.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Bydd yr Aelod yn ymwybodol fod—[Torri ar draws.] Bydd yr Aelod yn ymwybodol fod gennym broses symleiddio yng Nghymru, sydd i fod i sicrhau bod ganddynt swyddi, fod gan nyrsys a bydwragedd ac eraill swyddi pan fyddant yn graddio. Yn anffodus, oherwydd methiant y Llywodraeth flaenorol i anrhydeddu hyn, ni all llawer o nyrsys, bydwragedd a pharafeddygon yng Nghymru heddiw gael mynediad at y swyddi hynny, a dyna pam y gwnaethom sefydlu'r uwchgynhadledd graddedigion. Felly, nid wyf am ailadrodd yr ateb hwnnw eto; rwyf wedi'i ateb unwaith eisoes, felly maddeuwch i mi os nad af ar drywydd hynny ymhellach.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm sorry to be a type of Job's comforter, as my dear mother would say, but I'm going to add to your woes—your already considerable pile of woes—sorry. The situation isn't just nurses and midwives, but it actually involves medical trainees as well, speaking, again, from an ophthalmic perspective, which takes seven to 10 years of training in blood, sweat, tears and vitreous, as well as the actual cost of it as well. And we lose a third of our trainees to England because there's a lack of centralised planning for consultant vacancies for when people leave the system. So, then what we end up with in Wales is—and we already have the lowest number of specialist consultant ophthalmologists in Britain per head—we recruit from abroad to fill up the gaps. Whereas if only we could have a centralised authority to match trainees with their jobs, we would solve the problem. So, do you agree that you need central planning on a specialty basis to stop the brain drain from our country?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n ddrwg gennyf fod yn fath o gysurwr Job, fel y byddai fy mam annwyl yn ei ddweud, ond rwy'n mynd i ychwanegu at eich trafferthion—eich pentwr sylweddol o drafferthion—mae'n ddrwg gennyf. Nid nyrsys a bydwragedd yn unig yw'r sefyllfa, mae'n cynnwys hyfforddeion meddygol hefyd, gan siarad, eto, o safbwynt offthalmig, sy'n galw am saith i 10 mlynedd o hyfforddiant caled yn ogystal â'r gost. Ac rydym yn colli traean o'n hyfforddeion i Loegr oherwydd bod diffyg cynllunio canolog ar gyfer swyddi meddygon ymgynghorol erbyn yr adeg pan fydd pobl yn gadael y system. Felly, yr hyn sydd gennym yng Nghymru yw—ac eisoes, gennym ni y mae'r nifer isaf o offthalmolegwyr ymgynghorol arbenigol y pen ym Mhrydain—rydym yn recriwtio o dramor i lenwi'r bylchau. Ond pe bai gennym awdurdod canolog i baru hyfforddeion â'u swyddi, byddem yn datrys y broblem. Felly, a ydych chi'n cytuno bod angen cynllunio canolog ar sail arbenigedd i atal y draen dawn o'n gwlad?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The Member is absolutely right that, in the ophthalmic field, as in many other fields in health and care, in fact, we have many vacancies. The truth is that the system as it is, the one that we found when we got into position, doesn't record fully the whole workforce that we've got in Wales. So, some of the gaps that we've got, we are dependent on other bodies to inform us of their best-case situation.

So, we have to rectify this and make sure that we know the current situation and, moving forward, know what we will need. That's why we've set up two plans. First of all, a clinical plan for Wales so that we understand what the clinical needs of Wales are moving forward, and sitting beneath that clinical plan, we will have, and are developing now, the full comprehensive workforce plan—and I've mentioned this in this Chamber before—where I will be producing the first high-level part of that workforce plan and bringing it forward to the Senedd in the autumn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Aelod yn hollol gywir fod gennym lawer o swyddi gwag yn y maes offthalmig, fel mewn llawer o feysydd eraill ym maes iechyd a gofal. Y gwir amdani yw nad yw'r system fel y mae, yr un a welsom pan ddaethom i mewn, yn cofnodi'n llawn yr holl weithlu sydd gennym yng Nghymru. Felly, yn achos rhai o'r bylchau sydd gennym, rydym yn dibynnu ar gyrff eraill i'n hysbysu ynghylch eu sefyllfa orau.

Felly, rhaid inni unioni hyn a gwneud yn siŵr ein bod yn gwybod beth yw'r sefyllfa bresennol ac wrth symud ymlaen, ein bod yn gwybod beth fydd ei angen arnom. Dyna pam ein bod wedi sefydlu dau gynllun. Yn gyntaf oll, cynllun clinigol i Gymru fel ein bod yn deall beth yw anghenion clinigol Cymru wrth symud ymlaen, ac o dan y cynllun clinigol hwnnw, bydd gennym, ac rydym yn ei ddatblygu nawr, y cynllun gweithlu cynhwysfawr llawn—ac rwyf wedi sôn am hyn yn y Siambr o'r blaen—lle byddaf yn cynhyrchu'r rhan lefel uchel gyntaf o'r cynllun gweithlu hwnnw ac yn ei gyflwyno i'r Senedd yn yr hydref.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, Swansea Bay University Health Board has recruited over 450 nurses from overseas in recent years. At the very same time, nurses graduating from Swansea University, who have completed thousands of hours of unpaid clinical training here in Wales, are unable to find employment within the Welsh NHS. We are training our own and then turning them away while recruiting from abroad to fill the gap. That cannot be sound workforce planning. So, Minister, why is the Welsh Government content to see Welsh graduates locked out of jobs while relying on overseas recruitment? Would it not be better to employ the nurses and midwives we have already trained here in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog, mae Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Bae Abertawe wedi recriwtio dros 450 o nyrsys o dramor yn ystod y blynyddoedd diwethaf. Ar yr un pryd, nid yw nyrsys sy'n graddio o Brifysgol Abertawe, sydd wedi cwblhau miloedd o oriau o hyfforddiant clinigol di-dâl yma yng Nghymru, yn gallu dod o hyd i waith yn GIG Cymru. Rydym yn hyfforddi ein pobl ni ac yna'n eu troi ymaith wrth recriwtio o dramor i lenwi'r bwlch. Ni all hynny fod yn gynllunio gweithlu cadarn. Felly, Weinidog, pam y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn fodlon gweld graddedigion o Gymru'n cael eu cloi allan o swyddi gan ddibynnu ar recriwtio o dramor? Oni fyddai'n well cyflogi'r nyrsys a'r bydwragedd rydym eisoes wedi'u hyfforddi yma yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
This is slightly frustrating, because you're talking about two different things there that are going on. So, the situation with graduates, that goes back to 2022-23 and it will take a few years to work through the system. So, that's why we're finding an issue with the graduates now, because they started on their courses in 2022 when there were vacancies in the system, and the mapping and the modelling suggested that there would be vacancies in the system, but retention has improved because of the economic situation that the country finds itself in, which means that those positions are no longer available. So, that's dating back to 2022, when we did have those vacancies.

And the issue with having Indian nurses—. And once again, you're going on about Indian nurses, let's make sure that we show gratitude for the work of the nurses that come into this country, who treat your loved ones, my loved ones; they are there working, treating people who are sick, making sure that our loved ones improve. They've been recruited over the last few years before this year's graduate issue was recognised as a problem, which is a problem that lies with the previous Government.

So, yes, that's why we had a graduate summit, in order to make sure that this doesn't happen again. And, as and when we need to recruit more nurses, and if those nurses aren't available in Wales, absolutely, if those nurses want to come and work with us here in Wales from India, then we will welcome them, because they are helping us out here in Wales. The same as we have a number of Nigerian and Filipino nurses and carers working in the system, helping our loved ones, and we should show gratitude for the work that they do.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae hyn ychydig yn rhwystredig, oherwydd rydych chi'n siarad am ddau beth gwahanol sy'n digwydd. Mae'r sefyllfa gyda graddedigion yn mynd yn ôl i 2022-23 ac mae'n mynd i gymryd ychydig flynyddoedd i weithio drwy'r system. Felly, dyna pam y mae gennym broblem gyda'r graddedigion nawr, am eu bod wedi dechrau eu cyrsiau yn 2022 pan oedd swyddi gwag yn y system, ac roedd y mapio a'r modelu'n awgrymu y byddai swyddi gwag yn y system, ond mae lefelau cadw staff wedi gwella oherwydd y sefyllfa economaidd y mae'r wlad ynddi, sy'n golygu nad yw'r swyddi hynny ar gael mwyach. Felly, mae hynny'n dyddio'n ôl i 2022, pan oedd gennym y swyddi gwag hynny.

A'r broblem gyda chael nyrsys Indiaidd—. Ac unwaith eto, rydych chi'n siarad am nyrsys Indiaidd, gadewch inni wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn dangos ein diolch am waith y nyrsys sy'n dod i'r wlad hon, sy'n trin eich anwyliaid chi, fy anwyliaid i; maent yno'n gweithio, yn trin pobl sy'n sâl, yn gwneud yn siŵr bod ein hanwyliaid yn gwella. Maent wedi cael eu recriwtio dros y blynyddoedd diwethaf cyn i fater graddedigion eleni gael ei gydnabod fel problem, sy'n broblem a grëwyd gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol.

Felly, dyna pam y cawsom uwchgynhadledd graddedigion, er mwyn gwneud yn siŵr nad yw hyn yn digwydd eto. A phan fydd angen inni recriwtio mwy o nyrsys, ac os nad yw'r nyrsys hynny ar gael yng Nghymru, yn hollol, os yw'r nyrsys hynny eisiau dod i weithio gyda ni yma yng Nghymru o India, byddwn yn eu croesawu, oherwydd maent yn ein helpu ni yma yng Nghymru. Yr un peth gyda'r nyrsys a gofalwyr niferus sydd gennym o Nigeria ac Ynysoedd Philippines yn gweithio yn y system, yn helpu ein hanwyliaid, a dylem ddangos ein diolch am y gwaith a wnânt.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Low staffing numbers increase the length of waiting lists across many NHS services, but expectant mothers cannot join waiting lists, because babies don't wait. The Royal College of Midwives tell me that we now have unsafe staffing levels in maternity services across Wales. The impact of this situation is very serious. Not having a good birth experience is bad enough, but in some cases, it leads to medical complications. These complications can, of course, have a devastating effect on babies, their parents and, indeed, NHS staff. As well as the human impact, the costs to the NHS in treating conditions arising from birth complications and maternity cases are vast. I understand that a single maternity case typically costs £5 million. I understand also that to employ the 70 midwifery graduates who have not yet been offered jobs would cost less than £3.5 million. Not employing those midwives—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae niferoedd staffio isel yn cynyddu hyd rhestrau aros ar draws llawer o wasanaethau'r GIG, ond ni all mamau sy'n disgwyl ymuno â rhestrau aros, am nad yw babanod yn aros. Mae Coleg Brenhinol y Bydwragedd yn dweud wrthyf fod gennym lefelau staffio anniogel mewn gwasanaethau mamolaeth ledled Cymru. Mae effaith y sefyllfa hon yn ddifrifol iawn. Mae peidio â chael profiad geni da yn ddigon gwael, ond mewn rhai achosion, mae'n arwain at gymhlethdodau meddygol. Gall y cymhlethdodau hyn gael effaith ddinistriol ar fabanod, eu rhieni, ac ar staff y GIG yn wir. Yn ogystal â'r effaith ddynol, mae'r costau i'r GIG o drin cyflyrau sy'n deillio o gymhlethdodau genedigaeth ac achosion mamolaeth yn enfawr. Rwy'n deall bod un achos mamolaeth fel arfer yn costio £5 miliwn. Rwy'n deall hefyd y byddai cyflogi'r 70 o raddedigion bydwreigiaeth nad ydynt wedi cael cynnig swyddi eto yn costio llai na £3.5 miliwn. Byddai peidio â chyflogi'r bydwragedd hynny—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiwn, Paul.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A question, Paul.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: —feels like a false economy with an unjustifiable human impact. Will the Minister commit to placing all this year's midwifery graduates in jobs and making a plan to return midwifery services to a safe staffing level?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: —yn teimlo fel economi ffug gydag effaith ddynol na ellid ei chyfiawnhau. A wnaiff y Gweinidog ymrwymo i sicrhau swyddi i'r holl raddedigion bydwreigiaeth eleni a gwneud cynllun i ddychwelyd gwasanaethau bydwreigiaeth i lefel staffio ddiogel?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The Member is absolutely right that we've seen a number of reports into maternity units and midwifery here in Wales that do highlight unsafe staffing levels and we have to get to grips with this. I'm glad that, for instance, recently, we've seen a new report by Audit Wales into Swansea bay show a significant improvement there, and that's to be welcomed. That's what we want to see, more improvement in those fields.

Once again, for fear of repeating myself, I'll say that the issues that we have with graduates this year lies with the fact that they started on their courses back in 2022 and it's a legacy of the previous Government we are now having to deal with. That is why I got that graduate summit together in order to bring together the RCM, HEIW and the health boards to try and find as many positions available as possible for those students, to make sure that those students who aren't midwives now do become full midwives when the time allows and when positions allow, and that we ensure that this doesn't happen again in the future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r Aelod yn hollol gywir ein bod wedi gweld nifer o adroddiadau ar unedau mamolaeth a bydwreigiaeth yma yng Nghymru sy'n tynnu sylw at lefelau staffio anniogel ac mae'n rhaid inni fynd i'r afael â hyn. Rwy'n falch ein bod, er enghraifft, wedi gweld adroddiad newydd yn ddiweddar gan Archwilio Cymru ar fae Abertawe yn dangos gwelliant sylweddol yno, ac mae hynny i'w groesawu. Dyna beth rydym eisiau ei weld, mwy o welliant yn y meysydd hynny.

Unwaith eto, a chan fentro ailadrodd fy hun, rwyf am ddweud bod y problemau sydd gennym gyda graddedigion eleni yn deillio o'r ffaith eu bod wedi dechrau ar eu cyrsiau yn ôl yn 2022 ac mae'n rhywbeth a adawyd ar ôl gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol rydym bellach yn gorfod delio ag ef. Dyna pam y cefais yr uwchgynhadledd graddedigion, er mwyn dod â Choleg Brenhinol y Bydwragedd, Addysg a Gwella Iechyd Cymru a'r byrddau iechyd at ei gilydd i geisio dod o hyd i gymaint o swyddi â phosibl i'r myfyrwyr hynny, i wneud yn siŵr bod y myfyrwyr nad ydynt yn fydwragedd nawr yn dod yn fydwragedd llawn pan fydd yr amser yn caniatáu a phan fydd swyddi'n caniatáu, a'n bod yn sicrhau nad yw hyn yn digwydd eto yn y dyfodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Health boards are responsible for the planning and delivery of health services at a local level to meet the needs of their local population, working with their key stakeholders and partners.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r byrddau iechyd yn gyfrifol am gynllunio a darparu gwasanaethau iechyd ar lefel leol i ddiwallu anghenion eu poblogaeth leol, gan weithio gyda'u rhanddeiliaid a'u partneriaid allweddol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Residents in my constituency are deeply concerned about the future of Maesteg Community Hospital. Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board has proposals for a new health and well-being centre that mean that services will be relocated from Maesteg, but the health board has confirmed that the new site will not house any community beds at the premises. Meanwhile, the health board says it has made no decisions regarding the future of the Maesteg Community Hospital site, effectively leaving both it and residents in the area in limbo, causing a great deal of distress. Will the Minister agree to meet with Cwm Taf Morgannwg health board to discuss how the continued availability of community beds in Maesteg can be protected? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae trigolion yn fy etholaeth i'n bryderus iawn am ddyfodol Ysbyty Cymunedol Maesteg. Mae gan Fwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg argymhellion ar gyfer canolfan iechyd a lles newydd sy'n golygu y bydd gwasanaethau'n cael eu hadleoli o Faesteg, ond mae'r bwrdd iechyd wedi cadarnhau na fydd y safle newydd yn gartref i unrhyw welyau cymunedol ar y safle. Yn y cyfamser, mae'r bwrdd iechyd yn dweud nad yw wedi gwneud unrhyw benderfyniadau ynglŷn â dyfodol safle Ysbyty Cymunedol Maesteg, gan ei adael ef a thrigolion yr ardal mewn limbo, gan achosi llawer o drallod. A wnaiff y Gweinidog gytuno i gyfarfod â bwrdd iechyd Cwm Taf Morgannwg i drafod sut y gellir sicrhau bod gwelyau cymunedol yn parhau i fod ar gael ym Maesteg? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I understand the strength of feeling around the Maesteg Community Hospital. I expect any service change to be developed transparently with local people in line with national guidance and underpinned by robust evidence, options appraisals and impact assessments. I'm clear that services must be safe, sustainable and fit for purpose for the local population. In its preferred option for the development of a new health and well-being centre, the health board has highlighted that there will be an increased level and increased range of services available from the new proposed site. This is in addition to closer transport links with a bus stop and railway station in close proximity.

The health board has also committed to undertake further collaborative work on the Maesteg hospital building to ensure it is not lost. I understand that the board has requested an engagement plan on this to be presented at the July board meeting this month, in addition to an update on the plan for community beds within the Bridgend council area, and I have already met with the chair of Cwm Taf health board in order to discuss these.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n deall cryfder y teimlad ynghylch Ysbyty Cymunedol Maesteg. Rwy'n disgwyl i unrhyw newid i'r gwasanaeth gael ei ddatblygu'n dryloyw gyda phobl leol yn unol â chanllawiau cenedlaethol ac wedi'i ategu gan dystiolaeth gadarn, arfarniadau o opsiynau ac asesiadau effaith. Rwy'n glir fod yn rhaid i wasanaethau fod yn ddiogel, yn gynaliadwy ac yn addas i'r diben i'r boblogaeth leol. Yn yr opsiwn y mae'n ei ffafrio ar gyfer datblygu canolfan iechyd a lles newydd, mae'r bwrdd iechyd wedi tynnu sylw at y ffaith y bydd lefel uwch ac ystod uwch o wasanaethau ar gael o'r safle arfaethedig newydd. Mae hyn yn ychwanegol at gysylltiadau trafnidiaeth agosach gyda safle bws a gorsaf reilffordd yn agos.

Mae'r bwrdd iechyd hefyd wedi ymrwymo i ymgymryd â gwaith cydweithredol pellach ar adeilad ysbyty Maesteg i sicrhau nad yw'n cael ei golli. Rwy'n deall bod y bwrdd wedi gofyn am gynllun ymgysylltu ar hyn i'w gyflwyno yng nghyfarfod bwrdd mis Gorffennaf y mis hwn, yn ogystal â diweddariad ar y cynllun ar gyfer gwelyau cymunedol yn ardal cyngor Pen-y-bont ar Ogwr, ac rwyf eisoes wedi cyfarfod â chadeirydd bwrdd iechyd Cwm Taf er mwyn trafod y rhain.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Gweinidog, in the case of Maesteg hospital that my colleague has referenced, Llais highlighted the strength of feeling locally about retaining community bed capacity, and, indeed, you've just referenced that strength of feeling. They also emphasised the importance of continued engagement with residents as proposals develop. There remains considerable worry locally about how alternative community provision, including step-down and respite care, will be delivered in practice.

I was grateful for your response earlier this month to a letter from myself and my fellow Plaid Cymru colleagues representing Afan Ogwr Rhondda, following the health board's decision to proceed with these proposals. In your reply, you noted that the Welsh Government officials would continue to engage with the health board as this work progresses. With that in mind, could you outline, please, what assurances the Welsh Government is seeking from Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board to ensure that any changes to community bed provision are supported by robust evidence, with solid working assumptions and meaningful engagement with local communities before any existing capacity is lost? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Weinidog, yn achos ysbyty Maesteg y cyfeiriodd fy nghyd-Aelod ato, tynnodd Llais sylw at gryfder y teimlad yn lleol ynglŷn â chadw capasiti gwelyau cymunedol, ac yn wir, rydych chi newydd gyfeirio at y cryfder teimlad hwnnw. Hefyd, roeddent yn pwysleisio pwysigrwydd ymgysylltu parhaus â thrigolion wrth i gynigion ddatblygu. Mae cryn bryder yn lleol ynglŷn â sut y bydd darpariaeth gymunedol amgen, gan gynnwys gofal cam-i-lawr a gofal seibiant, yn cael ei ddarparu yn ymarferol.

Roeddwn yn ddiolchgar am eich ymateb yn gynharach y mis hwn i lythyr oddi wrthyf i a fy nghyd-Aelodau Plaid Cymru sy'n cynrychioli Afan Ogwr Rhondda, yn dilyn penderfyniad y bwrdd iechyd i fwrw ymlaen â'r cynigion hyn. Yn eich ateb, fe nodoch chi y byddai swyddogion Llywodraeth Cymru yn parhau i ymgysylltu â'r bwrdd iechyd wrth i'r gwaith hwn fynd rhagddo. Gyda hynny mewn golwg, a allech chi amlinellu, os gwelwch yn dda, pa sicrwydd y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei geisio gan Fwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Cwm Taf Morgannwg i sicrhau bod unrhyw newidiadau i'r ddarpariaeth o welyau cymunedol yn cael eu cefnogi gan dystiolaeth gadarn, gan ragdybiaethau cadarn ac ymgysylltu ystyrlon â chymunedau lleol cyn y collir unrhyw gapasiti presennol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that question, and it reflects the strength of feeling in the Llynfi valley and other parts that are being served by the Maesteg hospital. And I understand that there are concerns around it; that's why I had that conversation with the chair of the health board in order to raise those concerns, concerns which have been raised in this Chamber, which I raised with the chair, making sure that they understood that that continued engagement is absolutely crucial, that they take on board the views of the residents, that we do get assurances that any decisions made are made by clinicians and are clinically led, and consider the distances of travel and the difficulty for some people to access some services in the area. So, we have to make sure, and health boards, especially when they present plans, have to make sure that these things are considered in the round and to the fullest possible extent in order to come to a decision.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am y cwestiwn hwnnw, ac mae'n adlewyrchu cryfder y teimlad yng Nghwm Llynfi a rhannau eraill sy'n cael eu gwasanaethu gan ysbyty Maesteg. Ac rwy'n deall bod pryderon yn ei gylch; dyna pam y cefais y sgwrs honno gyda chadeirydd y bwrdd iechyd er mwyn codi'r pryderon hynny, pryderon a godwyd yn y Siambr hon a godais innau gyda'r cadeirydd, gan wneud yn siŵr eu bod yn deall bod yr ymgysylltu parhaus hwnnw'n hollbwysig, eu bod yn ystyried safbwyntiau'r preswylwyr, ein bod yn cael sicrwydd fod unrhyw benderfyniadau a wneir yn cael eu gwneud gan glinigwyr ac yn cael eu harwain yn glinigol, ac yn ystyried y pellteroedd teithio a'r anhawster i rai pobl gael mynediad at wasanaethau yn yr ardal. Felly, rhaid i ni wneud yn siŵr, a rhaid i fyrddau iechyd, yn enwedig pan fyddant yn cyflwyno cynlluniau, wneud yn siŵr bod y pethau hyn yn cael eu hystyried yn eu cyfanrwydd ac i'r graddau mwyaf posibl er mwyn dod i benderfyniad.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Prynhawn da, Weinidog. The issue of community beds in our communities and our local areas is really important, as you'll know, and I just wanted to focus in on Powys. I know we've had a discussion about this, but you'll know that there was a leak recently that Powys Teaching Health Board is considering stripping in-patient beds from eight out of our 10 community hospitals. That means that we will lose them from Ystradgynlais, Llandrindod, Builth, Knighton, Bronllys, Welshpool, Llanidloes and Machynlleth. That's up to 146 beds gone in a county with no district general hospital, where the population is older, more rural and further from alternative care than anywhere else in the country. We already know, don't we, that hospital stays in Powys average 40 days against the nationally agreed ambition of getting that down to 21.

So, Cabinet Minister, I realise these plans are not confirmed as yet, but could I just ask for your views on these potential plans? And also, would you consider intervening, as did your equivalent in 2013 in Hywel Dda health board, when there was concern about a similar issue? Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Prynhawn da, Weinidog. Mae mater gwelyau cymunedol yn ein cymunedau a'n hardaloedd lleol yn bwysig iawn fel y gwyddoch, ac roeddwn i eisiau canolbwyntio ar Bowys. Rwy'n gwybod ein bod wedi cael trafodaeth am hyn, ond fe fyddwch yn gwybod ei bod wedi dod i'r amlwg yn answyddogol yn ddiweddar fod Bwrdd Iechyd Addysgu Powys yn ystyried cael gwared ar welyau cleifion mewnol o wyth o'n 10 ysbyty cymunedol. Mae hynny'n golygu y byddwn yn eu colli o Ystradgynlais, Llandrindod, Llanfair-ym-Muallt, Tref-y-clawdd, Bronllys, y Trallwng, Llanidloes a Machynlleth. Dyna hyd at 146 o welyau'n diflannu mewn sir heb ysbyty cyffredinol dosbarth, lle mae'r boblogaeth yn hŷn, yn fwy gwledig ac ymhellach i ffwrdd o ofal arall nag unrhyw le arall yn y wlad. Rydym eisoes yn gwybod, onid ydym, fod arosiadau ysbyty ym Mhowys yn 40 diwrnod ar gyfartaledd yn erbyn yr uchelgais y cytunwyd arno'n genedlaethol o'i gael i lawr i 21.

Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, rwy'n sylweddoli nad yw'r cynlluniau hyn wedi'u cadarnhau eto, ond a gaf i ofyn am eich safbwyntiau ar y cynlluniau posibl hyn? A hefyd, a wnewch chi ystyried ymyrryd, fel y gwnaeth Gweinidog arall yn 2013 ym mwrdd iechyd Hywel Dda, pan oedd pryder am fater tebyg? Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The health board has not yet made any decisions on its clinical services plan or any options for potential public consultation later this year, as this work remains under development. As part of the clinical services plan development process, the health board has been undertaking wider initial engagement across Powys over the last year, to help understand the strengths and weaknesses of current service provision and help inform and develop a future vision, potential models of care and options for change.

The clinical services plan will be a vital plan in delivering new ways of working that address critical service fragilities, ensuring services remain safe, sustainable, accessible and of high quality, which will have to be supported by evidence. The Welsh Government expects any service change to be developed transparently with local people in line with national guidance and underpinned by robust evidence, options appraisals and impact assessments to ensure services remain safe, sustainable and fit for purpose.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nid yw'r bwrdd iechyd wedi gwneud unrhyw benderfyniadau eto ar ei gynllun gwasanaethau clinigol nac unrhyw opsiynau ar gyfer ymgynghoriad cyhoeddus posibl yn ddiweddarach eleni, gan fod y gwaith hwn yn parhau i gael ei ddatblygu. Fel rhan o'r broses o ddatblygu'r cynllun gwasanaethau clinigol, mae'r bwrdd iechyd wedi bod yn cyflawni gwaith ymgysylltu cychwynnol ehangach ledled Powys dros y flwyddyn ddiwethaf, i helpu i ddeall cryfderau a gwendidau'r ddarpariaeth bresennol o wasanaethau a helpu i lywio a datblygu gweledigaeth yn y dyfodol, modelau gofal posibl ac opsiynau ar gyfer newid.

Bydd y cynllun gwasanaethau clinigol yn gynllun hanfodol ar gyfer darparu ffyrdd newydd o weithio sy'n mynd i'r afael â gwendidau critigol mewn gwasanaethau, gan sicrhau bod gwasanaethau'n parhau i fod yn ddiogel, yn gynaliadwy, yn hygyrch ac o ansawdd uchel, y bydd yn rhaid eu cefnogi gan dystiolaeth. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru'n disgwyl i unrhyw newid i wasanaethau gael ei ddatblygu'n dryloyw gyda phobl leol yn unol â chanllawiau cenedlaethol ac wedi'i ategu gan dystiolaeth gadarn, arfarniadau o opsiynau ac asesiadau effaith i sicrhau bod gwasanaethau'n parhau i fod yn ddiogel, yn gynaliadwy ac yn addas i'r diben.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Pa gymorth y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei ddarparu i helpu rhieni i ddychwelyd i'r gwaith yn dilyn diagnosis o gyflwr iechyd difrifol i blentyn? OQ64398
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What support is Welsh Government providing to help parents return to work following a diagnosis of a serious health condition for a child? OQ64398

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn. Rydyn ni’n gwybod bod rhieni sydd yn y sefyllfa hon yn aml yn wynebu sawl rhwystr i ddychwelyd i’r gwaith, a’r rhesymau hynny’n rhyng-gysylltiedig yn aml. Mae ein rhaglen Cymunedau am Waith a Mwy yn darparu mentor un-i-un i helpu rhieni i gael gafael ar becyn o gymorth a dolen gyswllt â rhwydweithiau lleol, er mwyn delio ag anghenion cyflogaeth yn ogystal ag amgylchiadau teuluol ehangach.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question. We know that parents in this situation often face multiple and interconnected barriers to returning to work. Our Communities for Work Plus programme provides a one-to-one mentor to help parents to access a package of support and links into local networks, to address both employment needs and wider family circumstances.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Weinidog. Last week, I met with Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, and I want to declare an interest: I have worked with this health board before when I worked at NHS Wales Performance and Improvement. So, last week, I met with Cardiff and Vale University Health Board's paediatric team to discuss the socioeconomic impact of a type 1 diabetes diagnosis in children and young people. I met with Ansruta Vijay Anand and Dr Ambika Shetty, and I'm very grateful for the work that they have both done in this area. Ansruta is a medical student, and she spoke to me about her research. Her findings were striking. In 68 per cent of cases where a child was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, there was a change to a parent's employment. This included reduced working hours, taking temporary leave from work and in some cases leaving employment altogether. And while this is recent research, I know that that anecdotally goes back decades as being other people's experiences as well. They also found that many children experience a significant delay in returning to school, nursery or other childcare settings following their diagnosis. Over the past decade, the number of children diagnosed with diabetes has increased by 29 per cent—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Yr wythnos diwethaf, cyfarfûm â Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro, ac rwyf am ddatgan buddiant: rwyf wedi gweithio gyda'r bwrdd iechyd hwn o'r blaen pan oeddwn i'n gweithio yn Perfformiad a Gwella GIG Cymru. Felly, yr wythnos diwethaf, cyfarfûm â thîm pediatrig Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro i drafod effaith economaidd-gymdeithasol diagnosis diabetes math 1 mewn plant a phobl ifanc. Cyfarfûm ag Ansruta Vijay Anand a Dr Ambika Shetty, ac rwy'n ddiolchgar iawn am y gwaith y mae'r ddwy wedi'i wneud yn y maes hwn. Myfyrwraig feddygol yw Ansruta, a siaradodd gyda mi am ei hymchwil. Roedd ei chanfyddiadau'n drawiadol. Mewn 68 y cant o achosion lle roedd plentyn wedi cael diagnosis o ddiabetes math 1, bu newid i gyflogaeth rhiant. Roedd hyn yn cynnwys llai o oriau gwaith, cymryd seibiant dros dro o'r gwaith ac mewn rhai achosion gadael cyflogaeth yn gyfan gwbl. Ac er mai ymchwil ddiweddar ydyw, rwy'n gwybod yn anecdotaidd fod pobl eraill hefyd wedi cael y profiadau hynny ers degawdau. Canfuwyd hefyd fod llawer o blant yn profi oedi sylweddol wrth ddychwelyd i'r ysgol, y feithrinfa neu leoliadau gofal plant eraill ar ôl iddynt gael diagnosis. Dros y degawd diwethaf, mae nifer y plant sydd wedi cael diagnosis o ddiabetes wedi cynyddu 29 y cant—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiwn, plis.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: A question, please.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Given this evidence, what work is the Welsh Government undertaking to support families following a child's diagnosis of type 1 diabetes? And can I thank every person who works in the NHS, regardless of where they were born, for the work that they do for us? Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: O ystyried y dystiolaeth hon, pa waith y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i gefnogi teuluoedd ar ôl i'w plentyn gael diagnosis o ddiabetes math 1? A gaf i ddiolch i bob unigolyn sy'n gweithio yn y GIG, ble bynnag y cawsant eu geni, am y gwaith y maent yn ei wneud er ein mwyn? Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to echo those sentiments put forward by the Member and thank the Member for bringing this to my attention. I welcome the research of Cardiff and Vale University Health Board on this issue. Clearly, the findings are sobering and shed new light on the insidious interrelationship between poor health and socioeconomics. We often talk about the social determinants of health and how they contribute to inequalities in health outcomes, but this study underlines that this dynamic can work both ways, whereby health conditions can, in and of themselves, lead to a deterioration in socioeconomic circumstances. 

We are committed to getting to grips with health-based inequalities. The Member will be aware that there is a first 100 days action on reviewing health-based inequalities in Wales, and I look forward to updating the Chamber on the findings. In the meantime, while the NHS does provide support packages to help families deal with a diagnosis and learn to manage their condition, including regular out-patient care by specialists, education programmes and technological solutions to reduce the burden of delivering insulin and monitoring glucose control, the evidence from the CVUHB research clearly shows that we must go further to strengthen these support mechanisms. I would welcome further engagement with both the Member and the researchers to understand how we can use these findings to learn, adapt and improve.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn adleisio'r teimladau a gyflwynwyd gan yr Aelod a diolch i'r Aelod am ddod â hyn i fy sylw. Rwy'n croesawu ymchwil Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro ar y mater hwn. Yn amlwg, mae'r canfyddiadau'n sobreiddiol ac yn taflu goleuni newydd ar y rhyngberthynas lechwraidd rhwng iechyd gwael ac economeg gymdeithasol. Rydym yn aml yn siarad am benderfynyddion cymdeithasol iechyd a sut y maent yn cyfrannu at anghydraddoldebau mewn canlyniadau iechyd, ond mae'r astudiaeth hon yn tanlinellu y gall y ddeinameg hon weithio'r ddwy ffordd, lle gall cyflyrau iechyd ynddynt eu hunain arwain at ddirywiad mewn amgylchiadau economaidd-gymdeithasol. 

Rydym wedi ymrwymo i fynd i'r afael ag anghydraddoldebau sy'n seiliedig ar iechyd. Bydd yr Aelod yn ymwybodol fod yna gam gweithredu 100 diwrnod cyntaf ar adolygu anghydraddoldebau ar sail iechyd yng Nghymru, ac edrychaf ymlaen at roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf i'r Siambr ar y canfyddiadau. Yn y cyfamser, er bod y GIG yn darparu pecynnau cymorth i helpu teuluoedd i ddelio â diagnosis a dysgu rheoli eu cyflwr, gan gynnwys gofal cleifion allanol rheolaidd gan arbenigwyr, rhaglenni addysg ac atebion technolegol i leihau'r baich o ddarparu inswlin a monitro rheoli glwcos, mae'r dystiolaeth o'r ymchwil gan Fwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Caerdydd a'r Fro yn dangos yn glir fod yn rhaid inni fynd ymhellach i gryfhau'r mecanweithiau cymorth hyn. Buaswn yn croesawu ymgysylltiad pellach â'r Aelod a'r ymchwilwyr i ddeall sut y gallwn ddefnyddio'r canfyddiadau hyn i ddysgu, addasu a gwella.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i sicrhau bod GIG Cymru yn defnyddio'r dechnoleg bresennol i gyflymu mynediad at ymgynghoriadau cleifion a gwasanaethau cysylltiedig? OQ64423
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. What action is the Welsh Government taking to ensure NHS Wales uses existing technology to speed up access to patient consultations and associated services? OQ64423

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Welsh Government is working with NHS Wales to make the most of existing technology to improve access to care. This includes strengthening the NHS Wales app, supporting virtual appointments and making use of ambient voice technology. Health boards and trusts are held to account on their performance to deliver patient outcomes and are expected to use existing technology as an enabler.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gweithio gyda GIG Cymru i wneud y gorau o'r dechnoleg bresennol i wella mynediad at ofal. Mae hyn yn cynnwys cryfhau ap GIG Cymru, cefnogi apwyntiadau rhithwir a defnyddio technoleg llais amgylchynol. Mae byrddau ac ymddiriedolaethau iechyd yn cael eu dwyn i gyfrif ar eu perfformiad yn cyflawni canlyniadau cleifion a disgwylir iddynt ddefnyddio technoleg sy'n bodoli fel galluogwr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: That's great to hear, because obviously face-to-face initial consultations are still vital for most people, but for those who have got long-term conditions or those who are working full time or have transport issues, online consultations are really going to work. We've referred to Betsi Cadwaladr. They did a trial of Attend Anywhere. There were five patients in 2020—five patients in five years, and they haven't told the public a single thing about how this technology is performing in north Wales. So, I agree with your sentiment that we know it's a vital part of services for the NHS, but in Betsi Cadwaladr, could you please tell me what is going on in terms of how they're using Attend Anywhere and other technology to help my constituents?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae hynny'n wych i'w glywed, oherwydd yn amlwg mae ymgynghoriadau cychwynnol wyneb yn wyneb yn dal i fod yn hanfodol i'r rhan fwyaf o bobl, ond i'r rhai sydd â chyflyrau hirdymor neu'r rhai sy'n gweithio'n llawn amser neu sydd â phroblemau trafnidiaeth, mae ymgynghoriadau ar-lein yn mynd i weithio. Rydym wedi cyfeirio at Betsi Cadwaladr. Fe wnaethant dreialu Attend Anywhere. Roedd pump o gleifion yn 2020—pump o gleifion mewn pum mlynedd, ac nid ydynt wedi dweud unrhyw beth wrth y cyhoedd ynglŷn â sut y mae'r dechnoleg hon yn perfformio yng ngogledd Cymru. Felly, rwy'n cytuno â'ch teimlad ein bod yn gwybod ei fod yn rhan hanfodol o wasanaethau'r GIG, ond yn Betsi Cadwaladr, a allech chi ddweud wrthyf beth sy'n digwydd o ran sut y maent yn defnyddio Attend Anywhere a thechnoleg arall i helpu fy etholwyr?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank the Member for bringing this to my attention. It seems to be another case of one of the pieces of best practice that we have in parts of health boards across Wales that just isn't realised or isn't shared, or sits on a shelf somewhere. We need to learn from any piece of good practice out there and ensure that it's rolled out. So, I will raise this with the health board. I'm happy to keep you in the loop on any response I get back, because if it's good and it works, then we need to ensure that others benefit from it.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i'r Aelod am ddod â hyn i fy sylw. Mae'n ymddangos ei fod yn achos arall o un o'r darnau o arferion gorau sydd gennym mewn rhannau o fyrddau iechyd ledled Cymru nad yw'n cael ei wireddu neu nad yw'n cael ei rannu, neu sy'n eistedd ar silff yn rhywle. Mae angen inni ddysgu o unrhyw ddarn o arfer da sydd i'w gael a sicrhau ei fod yn cael ei gyflwyno'n gyffredinol. Felly, byddaf yn codi hyn gyda'r bwrdd iechyd. Rwy'n hapus i'ch cadw chi'n hysbys ynghylch unrhyw ymateb a gaf yn ôl, oherwydd os yw'n dda a'i fod yn gweithio, mae angen inni sicrhau bod eraill yn elwa ohono.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
