XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Local Government Procurement

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i sicrhau bod caffael llywodraeth leol yn cefnogi busnesau Cymru ac yn gwneud y mwyaf o fanteision economaidd gwariant cyhoeddus yng Nghymru? OQ64389
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What steps is the Welsh Government taking to ensure that local government procurement supports Welsh businesses and maximises the economic benefits of public spending within Wales? OQ64389

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr, ac mae hwn eto'n gwestiwn pwysig. Mae'r Lywodraeth yma eisiau ein gweld ni'n gallu mynd ymhellach nag ydyn ni ar hyn o bryd yn y maes yma, a rhoi mwy o hyblygrwydd i lywodraeth leol ddefnyddio caffael i gefnogi busnesau Cymru a chryfhau cadwyni cyflenwi lleol. Dydy hwn ddim yn fy mhortffolio i'n uniongyrchol, ond dwi wedi chwilio am wybodaeth amdano fo. Felly, gobeithio y medraf i ateb eich ail gwestiwn chi.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, and, again, this is an important question. This Government does want to go further than we currently go in this area, and to provide greater flexibility to local government to use procurement to support Welsh businesses and strengthen local supply chains. This isn't directly in my portfolio, but I have sought information about it. So, I hope I can respond to your supplementary question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Minister. I've been approached by A.N. Richards, a well-established Welsh supplier based in Froncysyllte in my constituency, which has raised concerns about the increasing use of England-based procurement frameworks by Welsh local authorities, and the barriers steering procurement officers towards them. The company says the English procurement portal, used, in this case, for fleet purchasing, is more user friendly and efficient than its Welsh equivalent. As a result, procurement officers may be drawn towards England-based frameworks, creating a structural disadvantage for Welsh suppliers and undermining the Welsh Government's aim of maximising the economic benefit of public spending within Wales. What assessment has the Welsh Government made of the impact that the design and usability of Welsh procurement systems have on local authority procurement decisions? And what steps is it taking to improve Wales-based procurement routes and ensure more local authority spending is retained in the Welsh economy?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Weinidog. Mae A.N. Richards, cyflenwr Cymreig sefydledig yn Froncysyllte yn fy etholaeth, wedi cysylltu â mi, ac maent wedi codi pryderon ynghylch y defnydd cynyddol o fframweithiau caffael sydd wedi'u lleoli yn Lloegr gan awdurdodau lleol Cymru, a'r rhwystrau sy'n llywio swyddogion caffael tuag atynt. Dywed y cwmni fod porth caffael Lloegr, a ddefnyddir yn yr achos hwn ar gyfer prynu eu fflyd, yn haws ei ddefnyddio ac yn fwy effeithlon na'r porth cyfatebol yng Nghymru. O ganlyniad, gall swyddogion caffael gael eu denu at fframweithiau sydd wedi'u lleoli yn Lloegr, gan greu anfantais strwythurol i gyflenwyr Cymreig a thanseilio nod Llywodraeth Cymru o wneud y mwyaf o fudd economaidd gwariant cyhoeddus yng Nghymru. Pa asesiad y mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i wneud o'r effaith y mae cynllun a defnyddioldeb systemau caffael Cymru yn ei chael ar benderfyniadau caffael awdurdodau lleol? A pha gamau y mae'n eu cymryd i wella llwybrau caffael sydd wedi'u lleoli yng Nghymru a sicrhau bod mwy o wariant awdurdodau lleol yn cael ei gadw yn economi Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi am y cwestiwn atodol yna, ac mae'r Gweinidog perthnasol newydd gerdded i mewn i'r Siambr. [Torri ar draws.] O, ti ydy o. O, da iawn. Mae'r Gweinidog cyllid, felly, wedi clywed eich cais chi, a dwi'n deall, ar ôl holi am wybodaeth, fod yna ddatganiad polisi caffael newydd yn mynd i fod yn cael ei gyhoeddi yn adlewyrchu'r cynllun uchelgeisiol i gynyddu gwariant cyhoeddus yng Nghymru. Mae pethau wedi gwella, ac roedd yna Ddeddf caffael 2023, a basiwyd yn y Senedd yma, sydd wedi'i gwneud hi'n haws i fusnesau bach a chanolig gystadlu am gyfleoedd, ac i Fusnes Cymru, sy'n cynnig cymorth wedi’i deilwra i fusnesau Cymru i'w helpu nhw i ehangu, i dyfu a chryfhau, ac i ddeall y prosesau caffael cymhleth sydd yna. Ond dwi'n gwybod bod y Gweinidog cyllid yn awyddus iawn, fel ydw i, i fynd llawer iawn pellach o fewn ein grymoedd ni yn y Senedd yma. Felly, diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that supplementary question, and the relevant Minister has just walked into the Chamber. [Interruption.] Oh, it's you. Good. The finance Minister, rather, has heard your request, and, having sought information, I am given to understand that there will be a new procurement policy statement published to actually increase public expenditure in Wales. Things have improved, and there was the procurement Act 2023, passed in this Senedd, which has made it easier for SMEs to actually bid for opportunities, and for Business Wales, which provides tailored support for Welsh businesses to help them to expand, grow and strengthen, and to understand the complex procurement processes. But I do know that the Minister for finance is very eager, as am I, to go much further within our powers in this Senedd. So, thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that and obviously this will probably go to the financial Minister as well, so I'm going to carry on, as the Member just carried on. Small businesses are the backbone of our community in Wales, but many are effectively shut out of public sector contracts before the process has even begun. Large companies have dedicated teams to deal with procurement, legal requirements and lengthy tender documents. Small local businesses may have one person trying to do all of that while also running a day-to-day business. If the Welsh Government genuinely wants more public money to stay in Wales, it must make sure that local businesses have a fair chance to compete. So, my question is: what practical support will the Welsh Government provide to simplify the procurement process and help Welsh businesses bid successfully for local authority contracts? And will the Minister support publishing council-by-council figures showing how much public spending is awarded directly to Welsh businesses in respect of transparency? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am hynny ac yn amlwg mae'n debyg y bydd hyn yn mynd at y Gweinidog ariannol hefyd, felly rwy'n mynd i barhau, gan fod yr Aelod newydd barhau. Busnesau bach yw asgwrn cefn ein cymuned yng Nghymru, ond mae llawer ohonynt yn cael eu cau allan o gontractau'r sector cyhoeddus cyn i'r broses ddechrau hyd yn oed. Mae gan gwmnïau mawr dimau pwrpasol i ddelio â chaffael, gofynion cyfreithiol a dogfennau tendr hirfaith. Efallai y bydd gan fusnesau bach lleol un unigolyn sy'n ceisio gwneud hynny i gyd tra bydd hefyd yn rhedeg busnes o ddydd i ddydd. Os yw Llywodraeth Cymru o ddifrif eisiau i fwy o arian cyhoeddus aros yng Nghymru, rhaid iddi sicrhau bod busnesau lleol yn cael cyfle teg i gystadlu. Felly, fy nghwestiwn yw: pa gymorth ymarferol y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei ddarparu i symleiddio'r broses gaffael a helpu busnesau o Gymru i gynnig yn llwyddiannus am gontractau awdurdodau lleol? Ac a wnaiff y Gweinidog gefnogi cyhoeddi ffigurau'r cynghorau fesul un i ddangos faint o wariant cyhoeddus sy'n cael ei ddyfarnu'n uniongyrchol i fusnesau Cymru er budd tryloywder? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr am y cwestiwn yna ac am eich cefnogaeth chithau hefyd i gynyddu'r caffael cyhoeddus i fusnesau lleol. Mae rhywun yn gwybod bod yna waith i’w wneud yn y maes yma—gymaint o enghreifftiau lle dydy o ddim yn gweithio ar hyn o bryd. Fel dwi'n dweud, mae pethau wedi gwella ychydig, ond araf ydy pace y gwella yna ers pasio'r Ddeddf Partneriaeth Gymdeithasol a Chaffael Cyhoeddus (Cymru) yn 2023. Mae'r Ddeddf yna yn gosod dyletswydd ar awdurdodau contractio i wella llesiant economaidd cymdeithasol, amgylcheddol a diwylliannol drwy gaffael, gan gynnwys ystyried mynediad ar gyfer busnesau bach a chanolig, a hefyd gwaith teg yn cael sylw yn y Ddeddf yna.

Ond, wrth gwrs, mae yna le i fynd, fel rydych chi'n dweud. Dwi hefyd yn gobeithio y bydd y strategaeth bwyd newydd yn cyfarch rhan o hwn, oherwydd mae cynhyrchu bwyd yn lleol a chreu cadwyni cyflenwi lleol ar gyfer y sector cyhoeddus hefyd yn ffordd o atgyfnerthu busnesau lleol a’r sector amaethyddol ac yn y blaen. Felly, mae yna nifer o wahanol faterion medrith dod ynghyd yn fan hyn, gan gynnwys hefyd, wrth gwrs, y gwaith y bydd yr awdurdod ddatblygu cenedlaethol newydd yn gallu ei wneud i gefnogi busnesau er mwyn teimlo eu bod nhw'n cael mynediad at y contractau yma sydd yn cael eu cynnig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much for that question, and for your support too in increasing public procurement for local businesses. Now, we know that there is work to be done in this area—there are so many examples of where it isn't currently working. As I say, things have improved a little, but the pace of that improvement has been slow since the Social Partnership and Public Procurement (Wales) Act was passed in 2023. That legislation does place a duty on contracting authorities to improve economic, social, environmental and cultural well-being through procurement, including considering access for SMEs, and fair work is addressed in the legislation too.

But, of course, there is some way to go, as you say. I also hope that the new food strategy will address some of these issues, because local food production and creating local supply chains for the public sector again is a way of strengthening local businesses and the agricultural sector and so on. So, there are a number of different issues that can coalesce here, including, of course, the work that the national development body will do to support businesses so that they feel that they can access these contracts that are offered.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Tai Cymdeithasol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Social Housing

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i gyrraedd ei thargedau tai cymdeithasol? OQ64420
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What action is the Welsh Government taking to meet its social housing targets? OQ64420

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Rydym ni eisoes yn cymryd camau drwy'r grant tai cymdeithasol a rhaglen gyfalaf llety trosiannol. Mi fydd hyn yn mynd i'r afael â digartrefedd, yn lleihau dibyniaeth ar lety dros dro ac yn gwneud yn siŵr bod gan bobl ledled Cymru fynediad at gartrefi o safon sy'n effeithlon o ran ynni. Rydym ni hefyd yn sefydlu Unnos i gyflymu'r broses o ddarparu tai cymdeithasol ar draws Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. We are already taking action through the social housing grant and the transitional accommodation capital programme. This will tackle homelessness, reduce reliance on temporary accommodation and ensure that people across Wales have access to quality homes that are energy efficient. We're also establishing Unnos to accelerate the delivery of social housing across Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Minister. Following on from what our Reform spokesperson has already said, I would like to urge you further to have annual targets so that any progress on delivering those 20,000 social homes can be easily tracked. We all know that Rome wasn't built in a day, but we would like to know how many homes will be built in Wales in a year.

Minister, following alongside those aims to get people into social housing as soon as possible, I was wondering whether the pots of money currently given to registered social landlords to adapt old stock—current old stock—to meet the demand and needs of those on current waiting lists will continue.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Weinidog. Yn dilyn yr hyn y mae ein llefarydd Reform eisoes wedi'i ddweud, hoffwn eich annog ymhellach i gael targedau blynyddol fel y gellir olrhain unrhyw gynnydd ar ddarparu'r 20,000 o gartrefi cymdeithasol hynny yn hawdd. Rydym i gyd yn gwybod na chafodd Rhufain mo'i hadeiladu mewn diwrnod, ond hoffem wybod faint o gartrefi a gaiff eu hadeiladu yng Nghymru mewn blwyddyn.

Weinidog, ochr yn ochr â'r nodau i gael pobl i mewn i dai cymdeithasol cyn gynted â phosibl, roeddwn yn meddwl tybed a fydd y potiau o arian a roddir ar hyn o bryd i landlordiaid cymdeithasol cofrestredig i addasu hen stoc—hen stoc cyfredol—i ddiwallu galw ac anghenion y rhai sydd ar restrau aros presennol yn parhau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. Dwi'n deall y pwynt ynglŷn â chael targedau blynyddol, ond yn aml mae yna waith yn gallu digwydd tua diwedd y cyfnod. Felly, fuasai roi targedau blynyddol rigid mewn ffordd, felly, yr un un targed bob blwyddyn, ddim yn adlewyrchu realiti'r sefyllfa, achos dydy o ddim yn digwydd mewn ffordd linear. Yn aml iawn, mae'r broses yn cychwyn ac mae'r cyflymder yn digwydd tua diwedd y cyfnod. Ond mi wnaf i edrych i weld pa mor dryloyw—. Dwi eisiau bod yn dryloyw, a dwi am roi cymaint o wybodaeth i chi ag sy’n bosib. Dwi’n mynd i fod yn gofyn rŵan i fod yn rhan weithredol o rai o’r cyfarfodydd yma sydd yn digwydd efo’r gweision sifil imi gael deall yn union beth sydd yn mynd ymlaen.

Ac o ran y cymdeithasau tai yn dod â hen stoc i fyny i bwrpas, mae yna grant arall ar gyfer hwnna, yr optimised retrofit scheme, sydd yn llwyddiannus iawn yn gwella cyflwr ein tai cymdeithasol ni. Mae eisiau cyflymu hynny, ac mae eisiau hefyd gweld y stoc yn y sector preifat yn gallu symud ymlaen hefyd, fel bod ansawdd ein tai ni ym mhob man ac ar draws pob deiliadaeth yn gwella.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much. I do understand the point about having annual targets, but often work can happen towards the end of the period. So, setting rigid annual targets, therefore, the same target every year, wouldn't reflect the reality of the situation, because it doesn't happen in a linear way. Often, the process starts and it accelerates towards the end of the period. But I will look to see how transparent—. I want to be transparent, and I want to provide you with as much information as possible. I'm going to be asking to have an operational role in some of the meetings that are happening with civil servants for me to understand exactly what's going on.

And in terms of the housing associations bringing old stock up to standard, there is another grant available for that, the optimised retrofit scheme, which is very successful in terms of improving the condition of our social housing. We need to accelerate that, and we also need to see the private sector stock progressing as well, so that the quality of our housing everywhere and across all tenacies improves.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Pa gynnydd mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi'i wneud tuag at sefydlu rhaglen ôl-osod niwtral o ran deiliadaeth? OQ64397
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What progress has the Welsh Government made towards establishing a tenure-neutral retrofitting programme? OQ64397

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Mae hwnna’n cario ymlaen yn daclus iawn o’r ateb diwethaf yna, achos mae yna gynnydd yn cael ei wneud, ac, yn sicr, yn ein maniffesto ni, byddwch chi'n cofio bod sefydlu rhaglen ôl-osod sydd yn niwtral o ran deiliadaeth yn hollbwysig. Felly, gobeithio bod hynny'n arwain at ail gwestiwn—dwi'n anghofio bod yna ail gwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. That takes us on very neatly from that previous response, because progress is being made, and, certainly, in our manifesto, you will recall that establishing a tenure-neutral retrofit programme was a crucial part of that. So, I hope that that will lead to a supplementary question—I forget that there's a supplementary question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I warmly welcome the Welsh Government's commitment to a national home retrofitting programme. Good housing is good health. Better-insulated homes will not only reduce energy bills and carbon emissions, they also improve people's health and reduce pressure on the NHS. Public Health Wales estimates that tackling excess cold in Welsh homes alone can save the NHS more than £40 million a year. Living in cold, damp and mouldy homes also increases the risk of respiratory illnesses, particularly in children and older people. So, Cabinet Minister, can you outline how the Welsh Government's retrofitting programme will prioritise tackling damp, mould and excess cold in homes so that it improves public health, reduces pressure on the NHS and lowers energy bills for families across Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n croesawu'n gynnes ymrwymiad Llywodraeth Cymru i raglen genedlaethol ar gyfer ôl-osod cartrefi. Mae tai da yn iechyd da. Bydd cartrefi wedi'u hinswleiddio'n well nid yn unig yn lleihau biliau ynni ac allyriadau carbon, maent hefyd yn gwella iechyd pobl ac yn lleihau'r pwysau ar y GIG. Mae Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru yn amcangyfrif y gall mynd i'r afael ag oerfel gormodol yn unig yng nghartrefi Cymru arbed mwy na £40 miliwn y flwyddyn i'r GIG. Hefyd, mae byw mewn cartrefi oer, llaith a llawn llwydni yn cynyddu'r risg o afiechydon anadlol, yn enwedig mewn plant a phobl hŷn. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, a allwch chi amlinellu sut y bydd rhaglen ôl-osod Llywodraeth Cymru yn blaenoriaethu mynd i'r afael â lleithder, llwydni ac oerfel gormodol mewn cartrefi fel ei bod yn gwella iechyd y cyhoedd, yn lleihau'r pwysau ar y GIG ac yn lleihau biliau ynni i deuluoedd ledled Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn. Mae yna nifer o resymau, onid oes, pam mae hi’n bwysig inni fod yn gwella cyflwr ein tai ni. Un rheswm ydy er mwyn eu datgarboneiddio nhw er mwyn ein bod ni yng Nghymru yn cyfrannu llai drwy ein tai ni tuag at newid hinsawdd. Mae tai yn cyfrannu 11 y cant o allyriadau carbon yng Nghymru ar hyn o bryd, a dwi'n awyddus iawn i weld hynna yn gostwng, ac mae cael cynllun i datgarboneiddio tai yn hollbwysig. Ond mae manteision ynglŷn â biliau, costau biliau yn dod i lawr oherwydd ein bod ni'n gwneud ein tai yn fwy ynni effeithiol—mae'n bwysig i ni edrych ar hynny—ac mae hefyd tlodi tanwydd yn broblem yng Nghymru, so mae o'n mynd i fod yn ein helpu ni i daclo tlodi. Ond hefyd mae'r effaith ar iechyd yn hollbwysig, a dwi yn cael trafodaethau efo'r Dirprwy Weinidog ar waith ataliol, oherwydd, i fi, mae tai yn hollol ganolog i wella iechyd pobl, ac mi fedrwn ni wella deilliannau iechyd ein gwlad ni drwy roi ffocws clir ar wella cyflwr ein tai ni. Dwi'n mynd dydd Iau i weld—tŷ cymdeithasol ydy o—sut mae'r cynlluniau gwella wedi helpu teulu penodol yn y fanna, ac mi fyddaf i'n gwneud mwy o gyhoeddiadau ynglŷn â'r maes penodol yma hefyd yn y 100 diwrnod cyntaf.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. There are a number of reasons why it's important that we improve the standard of our housing. One is to decarbonise so that we in Wales contribute less to climate change through our housing sector. Housing contributes around 11 per cent of carbon emissions in Wales, and I am very eager to see that reduced, and having a plan to decarbonise homes is very important. But there are benefits in terms of reducing bills as a result of making our homes more energy efficient—it's important that we consider that—and fuel poverty is also an issue in Wales, and it'll help us tackle poverty more generally. But also there is the impact on health, which is crucially important, and I am having discussions with the Deputy Minister in relation to preventative work, because, for me, housing is central to improving people's health, and we can improve health outcomes for our nation by having a clear focus on improving our housing standards. I will be going on Thursday to see—it's social housing—how retrofit programmes have helped a particular family there, and I'll be making further announcements on this specific area in our first 100 days.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. And the last question, Minister, Anna Nicholl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Mi wnes i drafod yr adolygiad penodol yma ar y fformiwla gyllido efo'r is-grŵp cyllid ar 8 Gorffennaf. Yr is-grŵp cyllid ydy'r is-grŵp o dan y WLGA sydd yn ymdrin â'r materion yma.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. I discussed this particular review of the funding formula with the finance sub-group on 8 July. The finance sub-group is the sub-group of the WLGA dealing with these issues.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Mae Ceredigion a sir Benfro ymysg yr awdurdodau mwyaf gwledig Cymru. Mae pobl yng Nghymru wledig yn wynebu costau byw uwch tra, yn aml, yn ennill cyflogau is, ac mae poblogaeth sy'n heneiddio yn cynyddu'r pwysau ar wasanaethau cyhoeddus sydd yn barod dan straen enfawr. Am rhy hir, mae cynghorau gwledig wedi gorfod gwneud mwy gyda llai. Nid yw'r fformiwla cyllid presennol yn adlewyrchu'r gwir gost o ddarparu gwasanaethau ar draws cymunedau gwledig gwasgaredig. Mae angen bargen deg ar gynghorau gwledig. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet, felly, ymrwymo i weithio mewn partneriaeth gyda chynghorau gwledig drwy gydol yr adolygiad fformiwla cyllid yma?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. Ceredigion and Pembrokeshire are among the most rural authorities in Wales. People in rural Wales face higher living costs while often earning lower wages, and an ageing population is increasing the pressure on public services that are already under immense strain. For too long, rural councils have had to do more with less. The current funding formula does not reflect the true cost of delivering services across dispersed rural communities. Rural councils need a fair deal. Will the Cabinet Minister, therefore, commit to working in partnership with rural councils throughout this funding formula review?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Gwnaf. Gwnaf i ymrwymo i weithio nid yn unig efo cynghorau gwledig, ond efo cynghorau ar draws Cymru—cynghorau trefol hefyd, oherwydd dwi yn hollol glir mai gwaith rydym ni'n ei wneud efo'n gilydd ydy hwn. Fel rydych chi'n sôn, mae'r agwedd wledig yn un bwysig, ond mae amddifadedd yn bwysig hefyd, ac, wrth gwrs, mae amddifadedd yn digwydd hefyd mewn ardaloedd gwledig.

Pwrpas yr adolygiad ydy ceisio gweld a oes angen newid, ac, os ydym ni'n mynd i newid, fod hynny'n adlewyrchu'n deg yr anghenion ar draws Cymru mewn gwahanol feysydd. Mae'r gwaith wedi dechrau ac, hyd yma, mae arweinwyr cyngor wedi bod yn rhoi mewnbwn adeiladol iawn i mewn i'r gwaith, ac mi fyddwn ni'n para efo'r gwaith. Mi fyddwn ni'n comisiynu adolygiad allanol i wneud yn siŵr bod y dystiolaeth yn gywir a bod y gwaith yn digwydd mewn ffordd sydd yn dryloyw ac i bawb gael deall beth sydd yn mynd ymlaen. Felly, dwi'n edrych ymlaen at weld ffrwyth y gwaith yna hefyd. Byddan nhw'n edrych ar brofiadau mewn gwledydd eraill—yn ogystal â rhoi ffocws ar Gymru, byddan nhw'n edrych i weld sut mae fformiwlâu dosbarthu yn gweithio mewn gwledydd eraill. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I will. I will commit to work not only with the rural councils, but with councils across Wales—urban councils too, because I am entirely clear that this is work that should be undertaken collaboratively. As you mentioned, the rural aspect is important, but deprivation is also important, and there is, of course, deprivation in rural areas too.

Now, the purpose of the review is to decide whether change is needed, and, if we are to make changes, that that fairly reflects needs across Wales in different areas. The work has commenced, and, to date, the council leaders have been providing very constructive input to that work, and we will continue with that work. We will be commissioning an external review in order to ensure that the evidence is accurate and that the work is happening in a way that is transparent, and that everyone can understand what is happening. So, I look forward to seeing that bear fruit too. They will be looking at experiences in other countries—as well as focusing on Wales, they will look to see how distribution formulas work in different countries. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Mae'r tân bellach dan reolaeth, a diolch i ymdrechion Gwasanaeth Tân ac Achub Gogledd Cymru a'r holl bartneriaid. Mae hyn yn ein hatgoffa ni o fygythiad newid hinsawdd a'r angen i bob gwasanaeth cyhoeddus addasu i hynny.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. The fire is under control now, thanks to the efforts of the North Wales Fire and Rescue Service and all of the partners. This reminds us of the climate change threat and the need for all public services to adapt to that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Mae'r golygfeydd brawychus a gwelsom ar fynydd Conwy dros y penwythnos nid yn unig wedi cael effaith uniongyrchol ar drigolion, cymunedau, ffermwyr, busnesau lleol a byd natur, ond maent hefyd wedi codi cwestiynau difrifol ynglŷn â'r effaith gwirioneddol mae newid hinsawdd yn ei gael ar y blaned.

Hoffwn ddechrau drwy roi ar y cofnod unwaith eto fy niolch diffuant i'r gwasanaethau brys, yr awdurdod lleol ac i gymunedau cyfagos am eu hymateb cyflym a phendant yn wyneb yr argyfwng dros y dyddiau diwethaf. Ddirprwy Lywydd, fel y soniais yn y Siambr ddoe, rwy'n falch bod y gwaethaf o'r argyfwng y tu ôl i ni erbyn hyn. Serch hynny, mae nifer o fy etholwyr yn dal i ofyn cwestiynau am beth fydd yr ymateb, rŵan, i'r difrod a'r heriau a grëwyd gan y tân gwyllt. Gwerthfawrogwn, felly, pe gallai'r Gweinidog Cabinet roi mwy o fanylion ar sut bydd Llywodraeth Cymru'n cydlynu ymdrechion gyda'r rhanddeiliad lleol i ddechrau ar y gwaith o ail-adfer y 200 erw o dir amaethyddol a choedwigol a ddifethwyd. Hoffwn hefyd wybod os bydd mesurau'n cael eu cyflwyno i warchod trigolion sydd gyda phroblemau anadlu a resbiradaeth yn sgil y difrod a wnaed i ansawdd aer yr ardal leol.

Ac yn olaf, bydd digwyddiadau'r penwythnos yn sicr wedi bod yn ergyd i ffermwyr a busnesau lleol. Byddwn yn gwerthfawrogi, felly, pe gallai'r Gweinidog sôn am unrhyw gymorth fydd ar gael i'w cefnogi nhw. Ac fel y dywedais ynghynt, dylem ni i gyd yn y Siambr hon fod yn bryderus o'r hyn mae digwyddiadau ar fynydd Conwy, ynghyd â digwyddiadau tebyg yng nghoedwig Braichmelyn ym Methesda, yn ei ddweud wrthym am fygythiad dirfodol newid hinsawdd. Roeddwn yn falch o glywed y Trefnydd yn cytuno ddoe fod angen cynllun mwy cynhwysfawr yn ei le ar gyfer digwyddiadau tebyg yn y dyfodol. Gwerthfawrogwn, felly, pe gallai'r Gweinidog Cabinet ymhelaethu ychydig ar ba fesurau bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cyflwyno i atal digwyddiadau tebyg rhag bod yn gyffredin ar draws Cymru, a sicrhau ein bod ni wedi paratoi gymaint â phosib, os ydy digwyddiadau fel hyn yn codi yn y dyfodol. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you, Minister. The frightening sights that we saw on Conwy mountain over the weekend have not only had a direct impact on residents, communities, farmers, local businesses and nature, but they have also raised serious questions about the very real impact that climate change is having on the planet.

I'd like to start by placing on record once again my sincere thanks to the emergency services, the local authority and to nearby communities for their swift and determined response in the face of the crisis over recent days. Dirprwy Lywydd, as I mentioned in the Chamber yesterday, I'm pleased that the worst of the crisis is now behind us. However, many of my constituents are still asking questions about what the response will be to the damage and challenges posed by this wildfire. I would appreciate, therefore, if the Cabinet Minister could provide further details on how the Welsh Government will co-ordinate efforts with local stakeholders to start the work of restoring the 200 acres of agricultural and forestry land that was destroyed. I'd also like to know if measures will be put in place to safeguard residents who have respiratory problems as a result of the damage done to air quality in the local area.

And finally, the events of the weekend will have certainly been a blow to farmers and local businesses. I would appreciate it, therefore, if the Minister could tell us of any support that may be available to support them. And as I said earlier, we should all in this Chamber be concerned about what the events on the Conwy mountain, as well as similar incidents at Braichmelyn forest in Bethesda, tell us about the existential threat of climate change. I was pleased to hear the Trefnydd agree yesterday that we need a more comprehensive plan in place for such incidents in the future. I would appreciate, therefore, if the Cabinet Minister could expand on what measures the Welsh Government will put in place to prevent such incidents from becoming common across Wales, and to ensure that we are as well prepared as possible if these incidents do arise in future. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi am ddod â'r mater yma gerbron y Senedd. Mae rhywun yn meddwl am y bobl gafodd eu heffeithio gan y tân yma. Dwi ond yn gallu dychmygu gymaint o ofn roedden nhw'n byw ynddo fo yn ystod y cyfnod yna pan oedd y fflamau yn rhuo ar y mynydd ym Mhenmaenmawr, ardal dwi'n gyfarwydd iawn â hi. Mi fu'n rhaid i 36 o aelwydydd adael eu cartrefi yn ystod y gwaith diffodd y tân, ond yn lwcus mi oedd modd iddyn nhw fynd yn ôl adref nos Lun. Mi wnaeth cyngor Conwy ddarparu llety dros dro i'r rhai oedd ei angen, felly rydyn ni'n hynod o ddiolchgar i gyngor Conwy am eu gwaith nhw ac yn ddiolchgar i Gyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, ond wrth gwrs i'r gwasanaeth tân. Mae ymladd tanau gwyllt yn waith hynod o anodd a pheryglus, ac mae eisiau talu teyrnged i holl ddiffoddwyr tân y gogledd a'r asiantaethau partner sydd wedi gweithredu mor gyflym i ymateb i'r digwyddiad yma a chadw pobl a chymunedau yn ddiogel.

Rydych chi'n holi pa gefnogaeth gall Llywodraeth Cymru ei rhoi. Wel, wrth gwrs, rydyn ni'n gweithio efo'r partneriaid lleol. Y cyngor sir ydy'r lle cyntaf, debyg, i fod yn deall beth ydy'r problemau sydd efallai'n parhau rŵan oherwydd beth sydd wedi digwydd, a hefyd Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru ynglŷn ag adfer y tir ac unrhyw waith sydd angen digwydd o ran yr ochr natur o bethau. Ond rydych chi'n iawn, mae hwn yn ein dychryn ni ac yn gwneud i ni sylweddoli difrifoldeb y sefyllfa o ran yr hinsawdd, yr argyfwng natur a hinsawdd rydyn ni'n wynebu yma. Dwi ddim yn meddwl y medrith neb ddechrau bod yn gwadu bod hwnna yn real iawn. Rhwng y tanau yma, rhwng y gwres llethol yma, sydd hefyd yn effeithio pobl mewn ffyrdd sydd yn negyddol iawn, mae'n rhaid i ni yn wirioneddol daclo'r argyfwng sydd yn ein hwynebu ni yng Nghymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much for bringing this issue forward before the Senedd. One thinks about the people who were affected by this fire. I can only imagine how frightened they must have been during that period when the flames were roaring on the mountain in Penmaenmawr, an area I've very familiar with. Thirty-six households had to flee their homes during the work of putting out the fire, but luckily they could return home on Monday evening. Conwy council provided temporary accommodation for those who needed it, so we are very grateful to Conwy council for their work and very grateful to Natural Resources Wales, and, of course, to the fire service. Fighting wildfires is very difficult and dangerous work, and we need to pay tribute to all the firefighters in north Wales and the partner agencies who responded so quickly to this event and kept communities and people safe.

You asked what support the Welsh Government can provide. Well, of course, we are working with local partners. The county council is in all likelihood the first port of call in terms of understanding the problems that may continue now because of what's happened, and also NRW in terms of restoring the land and any work that needs to happen on the nature side of things. But you're right, this is shocking and makes us realise the severity of the situation in terms of the climate, the nature emergency and climate emergency that we're facing here. I don't think anybody could start to deny that that's very real. Between these fires and this incredible heat that we've had, which is also affecting people in very negative ways, we genuinely have to tackle this crisis facing us in Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for your question, and I'm glad that—.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am eich cwestiwn, ac rwy'n falch bod—.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n falch eich bod chi yn poeni yr un fath â fi am y twf mewn tanau gwyllt, nid yn unig yn eich etholaeth chi ond ar draws Cymru. Mae'r Cabinet, y Llywodraeth, yr wythnos yma wedi bod yn trafod ein cynllun carbon ni fel Llywodraeth, sut ydyn ni yng Nghymru yn mynd i fod yn cyfrannu tuag at y dasg anferth, nid yn unig o daclo newid hinsawdd ond o liniaru ac addasu, fel rydych chi'n sôn. Dwi ddim yn siŵr beth mae'r Alban wedi'i wneud yn union, ond yn sicr mi fyddwn ni'n edrych ar hynny.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I am pleased that you, like me, are concerned about the growth in the number of wildfires, not only in your constituency but across the whole of Wales. The Cabinet, the Government, this week have been discussing our carbon plan as a Government, how we in Wales will contribute to the huge task  of not only of tackling climate change, but also mitigating and adapting to it, as you've mentioned. I'm not sure exactly what Scotland has done, but we will certainly look at that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Mair, for putting your question in. We actually did table an emergency question ourselves, the Welsh Conservatives, first thing on Monday morning; somehow that seems to have been rejected. But I'm glad that you put one in as well. So, I would like to endorse all the thanks that have gone before me: North Wales Fire and Rescue Service, Conwy County Borough Council and other partner agencies. Their incredibly fast response saved considerably more acres.

I'd also like to pay tribute to local residents who evacuated quickly, but also did what they could to try and help. It could have been far more serious, though it was incredibly serious in itself. Our farmer, Gareth Wyn Jones, who had to go himself in searing heat to try and rescue pigs from up on the uplands. The impact that this fire has had on local residents who have been forced out of their homes, there have to be questions now, asking how we can support them, because it's a frightening experience. There were 36 homes evacuated, one family noting it was actually in their driveway, and 200 acres of land have been affected.

We all have to be cautious. I wonder whether some messaging could go out in terms of graphics or something. Do you know, you only need, these days, glass? If you're carrying clear glass on hot, dry grass, it can easily turn into a fire. Not a fully extinguished cigarette butt: we should not be having people, you know—. They can unintentionally spark a fire, leading to significant damage whilst also putting lives at risk.

It was a very, very resource-intensive, financial-resource-intensive operation for all those partner agencies. I suppose what I'm asking for is: will you put some resources forward now for the aftermath of this? Will you contact those partner agencies and see how your Government can financially support them? But we also need a strategic plan. I'm not a lover of strategic plans, but we need something in place, because this could happen again. We're only halfway through the summer; this could happen again and again, and I want to be sure that all those partner agencies and rescue services are not stuck for finance in any way, shape or form. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Mair, am roi eich cwestiwn i mewn. Fe wnaethom gyflwyno cwestiwn brys ein hunain, y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, y peth cyntaf fore Llun; rywsut mae'n ymddangos bod hwnnw wedi'i wrthod. Ond rwy'n falch eich bod chi wedi cyflwyno un hefyd. Felly, hoffwn gymeradwyo'r holl ddiolchiadau sydd wedi'u gwneud: Gwasanaeth Tân ac Achub Gogledd Cymru, Cyngor Bwrdeistref Sirol Conwy ac asiantaethau partner eraill. Achubodd eu hymateb anhygoel o gyflym lawer mwy o erwau.

Hoffwn dalu teyrnged hefyd i drigolion lleol a adawodd eu cartrefi'n gyflym, ond a wnaeth yr hyn a allent hefyd i geisio helpu. Gallai fod wedi bod yn llawer mwy difrifol, er ei fod yn anhygoel o ddifrifol ynddo'i hun. Ein ffermwr, Gareth Wyn Jones, y bu'n rhaid iddo fynd ei hun mewn gwres tanllyd i geisio achub moch o'r ucheldiroedd. Rhaid bod cwestiynau nawr yn sgil yr effaith a gafodd hyn ar drigolion lleol a orfodwyd i adael eu cartrefi, ac sy'n gofyn sut y gallwn eu cefnogi, oherwydd mae'n brofiad brawychus. Bu'n rhaid i bobl adael 36 o gartrefi, gydag un teulu'n nodi bod y tân yn eu dreif, ac fe effeithiwyd ar 200 erw o dir.

Rhaid i bawb ohonom fod yn ofalus. Tybed a allai negeseuon fynd allan ar ffurf graffeg neu rywbeth. Wyddoch chi, dim ond gwydr sydd ei angen arnoch? Os ydych chi'n cario gwydr clir ar laswellt poeth, sych, gall droi'n dân yn hawdd. Nid sigarét wedi'i diffodd yn llawn: ni ddylem fod yn cael pobl, wyddoch chi—. Gallant gynnau tân yn anfwriadol, gan arwain at ddifrod sylweddol a rhoi bywydau mewn perygl.

Roedd yn ymgyrch a gostiodd lawer mewn adnoddau ac arian i'r holl asiantaethau partner. Mae'n debyg mai'r hyn rwy'n gofyn yw: a fyddwch chi'n darparu adnoddau nawr yn sgil hyn? A fyddwch chi'n cysylltu â'r asiantaethau partner i weld sut y gall eich Llywodraeth eu cefnogi'n ariannol? Ond mae angen cynllun strategol arnom hefyd. Nid wyf yn hoff o gynlluniau strategol, ond mae angen rhywbeth arnom, oherwydd gallai hyn ddigwydd eto. Nid ydym ond hanner ffordd drwy'r haf; gallai hyn ddigwydd eto ac eto, ac rwyf am fod yn siŵr nad yw'r holl asiantaethau partner a'r gwasanaethau achub yn brin o gyllid mewn unrhyw ffordd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn, Janet, a dwi'n cyd-fynd efo chi. Y teulu yna lle roedd y tân yn agos iawn at eu cartref nhw, roedd hynny yn ddychrynllyd iawn, onid oedd? Mae'n rhy gynnar i wybod ar hyn o bryd beth wnaeth achosi'r tân penodol yma ar y mynydd ym Mhenmaenmawr. Fel arfer, mae'r tanau yma yn digwydd yn gynt yn y flwyddyn, onid ydyn? Maen nhw'n digwydd rhwng mis Mawrth a mis Mai, ond maen nhw yn gynyddol yn digwydd yn yr haf, sydd eto yn arwydd o'r newid hinsawdd sydd yn digwydd. Ac mi ydych chi'n iawn, dwi'n meddwl bod eisiau i ni gael y neges yna allan, bod eisiau i bobl fod yn hynod ofalus wrth ddefnyddio barbeciws, wrth daflu pennau sigaréts, wrth adael gwydr ar ôl—mae gwydr yn gallu tanio pan fydd haul arno fo, ac yn gallu lledaenu ar draws y llystyfiant sydd yn sych iawn yr adeg yma o'r flwyddyn, a dydyn ni ddim wedi cael fawr ddim glaw. Felly, fel roeddwn i'n dweud, mae eisiau i ni wirioneddol feddwl ein bod ni'n blaenoriaethu taclo'r newid hinsawdd, a'n bod ni'n meddwl am y lliniaru a'r addasu sydd angen digwydd i ni i gyd yn ein bywydau ni. O ran y gefnogaeth a'r cymorth ariannol, mi fydd swyddogion Llywodraeth Cymru yn siarad efo'r asiantaethau i gyd rŵan i weld lle'n union y medrwn ni fod yn helpu, beth yn union ydy goblygiadau y tân sydd wedi digwydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Janet, and I do agree with you. That family there, where the fire was very close to their home, that was very frightening, wasn't it? It's too early to know at present what caused this specific fire on the mountain in Penmaenmawr. Usually these fires happen earlier in the year, don't they? They happen between March and May, but they're increasingly happening in the summer now, which is also an indication of the climate change that is happening. And you're right, I think that we do need to get that messaging out that people need to be very careful when using barbecues, when discarding cigarette butts and when leaving glass behind—glass can cause a fire when there is sunlight on it, and that can spread across the vegetation, which is very dry at this time of year, and we've had very little rain. So, as I said, we really do need to think about prioritising tackling climate change, and think about the mitigation measures and the adaptations that we need to undertake in all our lives. In terms of the support and financial support, Welsh Government officials will be talking to all the agencies now to see exactly where we can help and what exactly the implications of the fire are.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Education and the Welsh Language
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Addysg a’r Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I made a written statement on Monday, announcing my intention to consult after the summer holidays on a 3.5 per cent pay award for teachers and leaders, and a 5 per cent pay award for unqualified teachers. I will provide additional funding to support local authorities and schools with implementing the pay award.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe wneuthum ddatganiad ysgrifenedig ddydd Llun, yn cyhoeddi fy mwriad i ymgynghori ar ôl gwyliau'r haf ar ddyfarniad cyflog o 3.5 y cant i athrawon ac arweinwyr, a dyfarniad cyflog o 5 y cant i athrawon heb gymhwyso. Byddaf yn darparu cyllid ychwanegol i gefnogi awdurdodau lleol ac ysgolion i weithredu'r dyfarniad cyflog.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. As you've indicated, you made that written statement on Monday, announcing that you would consult from September. This is later than stakeholders would like. As you're aware, there's previously been a commitment to consult ahead of the school holidays, so that teachers can receive their pay rise as soon as possible, although I do welcome your commitment to start the process earlier in future years.

As we discussed yesterday, the Welsh Government is now in a pay dispute with both school leadership unions in Wales, with pay as well as additional learning needs funding cited as the reasons for the dispute. It was really worrying to see the written statement issued immediately after the debate yesterday, saying there would be no money for ALN, even though the Welsh Government could allocate that money, as they are doing with their priorities. But it's crucial now that the Government gets around the table with trade unions in order to prevent industrial action in the autumn.

Can I ask the Cabinet Minister what steps you'll take to ensure that this dispute focused on pay and ALN is urgently resolved?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Fel rydych chi wedi nodi, fe wnaethoch y datganiad ysgrifenedig hwnnw ddydd Llun, gan gyhoeddi y byddech chi'n ymgynghori o fis Medi. Mae hyn yn hwyrach nag y byddai rhanddeiliaid yn ei hoffi. Fel y gwyddoch, cafwyd ymrwymiad o'r blaen i ymgynghori cyn gwyliau'r ysgol, fel y gall athrawon gael eu codiad cyflog cyn gynted â phosibl, ond rwy'n croesawu eich ymrwymiad i ddechrau'r broses yn gynharach yn y blynyddoedd i ddod.

Fel y trafodwyd ddoe, mae Llywodraeth Cymru bellach mewn anghydfod cyflog gyda'r ddau undeb arweinyddiaeth ysgolion yng Nghymru, gyda chyflog yn ogystal â chyllid anghenion dysgu ychwanegol yn cael eu nodi fel rhesymau dros yr anghydfod. Roedd yn bryderus iawn gweld y datganiad ysgrifenedig a gyhoeddwyd yn syth ar ôl y ddadl ddoe, yn dweud na fyddai arian ar gyfer ADY, er y gallai Llywodraeth Cymru ddyrannu'r arian hwnnw, fel y maent yn ei wneud gyda'u blaenoriaethau nhw. Ond mae'n hollbwysig nawr fod y Llywodraeth yn trafod gydag undebau llafur er mwyn atal gweithredu diwydiannol yn yr hydref.

A gaf i ofyn i'r Gweinidog Cabinet pa gamau y byddwch chi'n eu cymryd i sicrhau bod yr anghydfod hwn sy'n canolbwyntio ar gyflogau ac ADY yn cael ei ddatrys ar frys?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
If I can take the point on the pay award timings first: yes, it would have been easier to consult at an earlier point. She may have noticed that there was an election. There was a period when these consultations could not have gone ahead, which is precisely why I made the announcement on the 3.5 per cent pay award for teachers and 5 per cent for unqualified teachers, because in representations to me, they said very clearly that an early indication—admitting the consultation would need now to happen in the autumn—early certainty, and an early certainty for local government that funding would be available to pay for these pay rises, was the desire of the workforce. That's why I made that statement at that point.

On ALN, I think that we are revisiting a conversation from yesterday. As my colleague said earlier on, we are very aware of the pressures in funding on both local government and on schools, and I have no doubt that those will be continuing conversations. On ALN specifically, what we set out to do, in conversation with you—and I thought that we were talking about the same thing, which was how to arrive at a sustainable model for ALN. For a number of years, it has been clear that that is not where we are. We are constantly told, by parents, families, schools and local authorities, that the current system is facing significant difficulty, and it was on that basis that we presented an argument for £40 million this year, £40 million next year and at least £40 million in the third year, in order to bring us to a point where we had a sustainable ALN system that we could be proud of. You voted against that yesterday.

On the trade dispute itself, I was obviously disappointed to receive a letter from the NAHT and the Association of School and College Leaders, entering into a trade dispute, given that we have been working together and I have been committed to the social partnership now and throughout my career. And I hope that we can move forward quickly to resolve these issues. I remain committed to the social partnership, and I'm currently considering the issues and the response.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Os caf gymryd y pwynt ar amseriadau'r dyfarniadau cyflog yn gyntaf: fe fyddai wedi bod yn haws ymgynghori ar adeg gynharach. Efallai ei bod wedi sylwi bod etholiad wedi bod. Roedd yna gyfnod pan na allai'r ymgynghoriadau hyn fod wedi mynd rhagddynt, a dyna'n union pam y gwneuthum y cyhoeddiad ar y dyfarniad cyflog o 3.5 y cant i athrawon a 5 y cant i athrawon heb gymhwyso, oherwydd mewn sylwadau i mi, roeddent yn dweud yn glir iawn mai arwydd cynnar—gan gyfaddef y byddai angen i'r ymgynghoriad ddigwydd yn yr hydref nawr—sicrwydd cynnar, a sicrwydd cynnar i lywodraeth leol y byddai cyllid ar gael i dalu am y codiadau cyflog hyn, oedd dymuniad y gweithlu. Dyna pam y gwneuthum y datganiad ar y pwynt hwnnw.

Ar ADY, rwy'n credu ein bod yn ailadrodd sgwrs a gawsom ddoe. Fel y dywedodd fy nghyd-Aelod yn gynharach, rydym yn ymwybodol iawn o'r pwysau cyllidol ar lywodraeth leol ac ar ysgolion, ac nid oes gennyf unrhyw amheuaeth y bydd y rheini'n sgyrsiau parhaus. Ar ADY yn benodol, yr hyn roeddem yn bwriadu ei wneud, mewn sgwrs gyda chi—ac roeddwn i'n meddwl ein bod yn siarad am yr un peth, sef sut i gyrraedd model cynaliadwy ar gyfer ADY. Ers nifer o flynyddoedd, mae wedi bod yn amlwg nad dyna lle rydym ni. Dywedir wrthym yn gyson, gan rieni, teuluoedd, ysgolion ac awdurdodau lleol, fod y system bresennol yn wynebu anawsterau sylweddol, ac ar y sail honno y gwnaethom gyflwyno dadl dros £40 miliwn eleni, £40 miliwn y flwyddyn nesaf ac o leiaf £40 miliwn yn y drydedd flwyddyn, er mwyn dod â ni at bwynt lle byddai gennym system ADY gynaliadwy y gallem fod yn falch ohoni. Fe wnaethoch chi bleidleisio yn erbyn hynny ddoe.

Ar yr anghydfod ei hun, roeddwn yn amlwg yn siomedig o dderbyn llythyr gan Gymdeithas Genedlaethol y Prifathrawon a'r Gymdeithas Arweinwyr Ysgolion a Cholegau, yn cofnodi'r anghydfod yn ffurfiol, o ystyried ein bod wedi bod yn gweithio gyda'n gilydd a fy mod i wedi bod yn ymrwymedig i'r bartneriaeth gymdeithasol nawr a thrwy gydol fy ngyrfa. Ac rwy'n gobeithio y gallwn symud ymlaen yn gyflym i ddatrys y materion hyn. Rwy'n parhau i fod yn ymrwymedig i'r bartneriaeth gymdeithasol, ac rwy'n ystyried y materion a'r ymateb ar hyn o bryd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I welcome the Gweinidog's acknowledgement that improving educational outcomes requires meaningful engagement with teachers, ensuring they feel supported, valued and listened to. It is somewhat ironic that when similar pay uplifts were offered to teachers in previous years, under previous Governments, they did not attract the same level of scrutiny. For too long, Wales has faced persistent challenges in retaining teachers. If we are serious about raising standards, we must work in genuine partnership with our education workforce. Teachers are central to our education system and should be able to focus on teaching and supporting learners, rather than being overwhelmed by unnecessary pressures. Therefore, Gweinidog, at a time when teachers face growing demands and expectations, how will the Welsh Government work with teachers, unions and local authorities to ensure that the profession is properly supported, teacher well-being is prioritised and schools can attract and retain the staff they need?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n croesawu cydnabyddiaeth y Gweinidog fod gwella canlyniadau addysgol yn galw am ymgysylltu ystyrlon ag athrawon, gan sicrhau eu bod yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu cefnogi, eu gwerthfawrogi a'u clywed. Mae'n eironig braidd nad oeddent yn denu'r un lefel o graffu pan gafodd codiadau cyflog tebyg eu cynnig i athrawon mewn blynyddoedd blaenorol, o dan Lywodraethau blaenorol. Ers gormod o amser, mae Cymru wedi wynebu heriau parhaus gyda chadw athrawon. Os ydym o ddifrif ynglŷn â chodi safonau, rhaid inni weithio mewn partneriaeth go iawn â'n gweithlu addysg. Mae athrawon yn ganolog i'n system addysg a dylent allu canolbwyntio ar addysgu a chefnogi dysgwyr, yn hytrach na chael eu llethu gan bwysau diangen. Felly, Weinidog, ar adeg pan fo athrawon yn wynebu galwadau a disgwyliadau cynyddol, sut y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn gweithio gydag athrawon, undebau ac awdurdodau lleol i sicrhau bod y proffesiwn yn cael ei gefnogi'n briodol, fod lles athrawon yn cael ei flaenoriaethu ac y gall ysgolion ddenu a chadw'r staff sydd eu hangen arnynt?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr, and I think she's quite right to point to the value we put on the teaching profession, and we are determined to work in partnership. I have existing relationships with teachers and school leaders across Wales, and I am in constant dialogue, formally and informally, with them, and we have a great deal that we want to do together around workload, around retaining and recruiting teachers, around the ideas we have on literacy and numeracy and clarity of expectation, looking at the curriculum. These are things that the teaching profession has welcomed, and it is a continuing dialogue that will touch on all the areas the Member mentioned. It will include the unions and as wide as possible an input from the people who deliver on the ground and who matter to us.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr, ac rwy'n credu ei bod hi'n hollol iawn i dynnu sylw at y gwerth a roddwn ar y proffesiwn addysgu, ac rydym yn benderfynol o weithio mewn partneriaeth. Mae gennyf berthynas yn barod gydag athrawon ac arweinwyr ysgolion ledled Cymru, ac rwyf mewn deialog gyson â nhw yn ffurfiol ac yn anffurfiol, ac mae gennym lawer iawn yr ydym am ei wneud gyda'n gilydd o ran llwyth gwaith, cadw a recriwtio athrawon, y syniadau sydd gennym ar lythrennedd a rhifedd ac eglurder disgwyliadau, gan edrych ar y cwricwlwm. Mae'r rhain yn bethau y mae'r proffesiwn addysgu wedi'u croesawu, ac mae'n ddeialog barhaus a fydd yn cyffwrdd â'r holl feysydd y soniodd yr Aelod amdanynt. Bydd yn cynnwys yr undebau a mewnbwn mor eang â phosibl gan y bobl sy'n cyflawni ar lawr gwlad ac sy'n bwysig i ni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As a former teacher, I know first-hand the challenges facing our schools and the immense commitment shown by teachers and school leaders across Wales, and I'd like to thank Lynne Neagle for bringing forward this question. Of course, supporting teachers is vital, and fair pay is an important part of that, but we must also recognise that the pressures facing the profession go far beyond pay alone. There is workload, recruitment and retention, additional learning needs provision and the increasing demands placed on schools all requiring attention. I note that the NAHT, the school leaders' union, and the Association of School and College Leaders have now written to the education Minister, herself a former leader of the NAHT, to formally register a dispute with the Welsh Government over the pay settlement, alongside concerns with ALN funding. What makes this particularly significant is that neither union has previously been in a formal dispute with the Welsh Government; these are unprecedented circumstances. Therefore, can the Minister outline how the Welsh Government intends to rebuild consensus with these unions, resolve the issues that have led to this dispute, and what further action can be taken to support teachers and school leaders across Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel cyn-athrawes, rwy'n gwybod yn uniongyrchol am yr heriau sy'n wynebu ein hysgolion a'r ymrwymiad aruthrol a ddangoswyd gan athrawon ac arweinwyr ysgolion ledled Cymru, a hoffwn ddiolch i Lynne Neagle am gyflwyno'r cwestiwn hwn. Wrth gwrs, mae cefnogi athrawon yn hanfodol, ac mae cyflog teg yn rhan bwysig o hynny, ond mae'n rhaid inni hefyd gydnabod bod y pwysau sy'n wynebu'r proffesiwn yn mynd ymhell y tu hwnt i dâl yn unig. Mae llwyth gwaith, recriwtio a chadw, darpariaeth anghenion dysgu ychwanegol a'r gofynion cynyddol a roddir ar ysgolion i gyd yn mynnu sylw. Nodaf fod Cymdeithas Genedlaethol y Prifathrawon, undeb yr arweinwyr ysgolion, a'r Gymdeithas Arweinwyr Ysgolion a Cholegau bellach wedi ysgrifennu at y Gweinidog Addysg, sydd ei hun yn un o gyn-arweinwyr Cymdeithas Genedlaethol y Prifathrawon, i gofnodi anghydfod yn ffurfiol gyda Llywodraeth Cymru ynglŷn â'r setliad cyflog, ochr yn ochr â phryderon ynglŷn â chyllid ADY. Yr hyn sy'n ei wneud yn arbennig o arwyddocaol yw nad yw'r naill undeb na'r llall wedi bod mewn anghydfod ffurfiol gyda Llywodraeth Cymru o'r blaen; mae'r rhain yn amgylchiadau digynsail. Felly, a all y Gweinidog amlinellu sut y mae Llywodraeth Cymru'n bwriadu ailadeiladu consensws gyda'r undebau hyn, datrys y materion sydd wedi arwain at yr anghydfod hwn, a pha gamau pellach y gellir eu cymryd i gefnogi athrawon ac arweinwyr ysgolion ledled Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, and I'm sure the former Minister will be grateful for your support. On the trade dispute, I am anxious to resolve this as quickly as possible, as I said earlier on, and I remain committed to working in social partnership with them. I think there is ground that we can build on here and I am determined to resolve that matter as quickly as I can.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, ac rwy'n siŵr y bydd y cyn-Weinidog yn ddiolchgar am eich cefnogaeth. O ran yr anghydfod, rwy'n awyddus i'w ddatrys cyn gynted â phosibl, fel y dywedais yn gynharach, ac rwy'n parhau i fod yn ymrwymedig i weithio mewn partneriaeth gymdeithasol gyda nhw. Rwy'n credu bod tir y gallwn adeiladu arno yma ac rwy'n benderfynol o ddatrys y mater cyn gynted ag y gallaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm grateful to Lynne Neagle for tabling this item here today. As you know, Cabinet Minister, schools across Wales are increasingly feeling overlooked and undervalued when it comes to funding. And, of course, you've already noted the serious challenges surrounding funding for additional learning needs, with many schools struggling to provide the support that learners deserve.

You've again mentioned the offer from the Welsh Government of that £40 million per year. But let's not forget that, last night, this Senedd rejected that as an option, because this Senedd believed that that was not enough to support ALN across Wales. And now we're seeing again a Welsh Government unwilling to meet the recommended pay award for teachers. It goes back to that point of them feeling overlooked and undervalued. Cabinet Minister, we cannot risk a strike in the autumn because of this situation.

I think that what's happening at the moment really sends the wrong message to a profession that's already feeling that immense pressure. Teachers, as already described by your Plaid Cymru colleague, are at the heart of our education system and there's a real risk of this general issue around funding affecting recruitment, retention and ultimately outcomes for our children and young people.

I'm particularly concerned about how school leaders are having to manage this situation at the moment, and I declare an interest as a school governor myself. School governing bodies are having to manage stretched budgets, and if schools are left to bridge the funding gap themselves, it's children who ultimately feel the impact of this. So, Cabinet Minister, can you explain what reassurance you can give headteachers and governing bodies that they won't have to choose between rewarding their staff fairly and appropriately and protecting the support and opportunities available to pupils?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n ddiolchgar i Lynne Neagle am gyflwyno'r eitem hon yma heddiw. Fel y gwyddoch, Weinidog Cabinet, mae ysgolion ledled Cymru yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu hanwybyddu a'u tanbrisio fwyfwy o ran cyllid. Ac wrth gwrs, rydych chi eisoes wedi nodi'r heriau difrifol o ran cyllid ar gyfer anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, gyda llawer o ysgolion yn ei chael hi'n anodd darparu'r gefnogaeth y mae dysgwyr yn ei haeddu.

Rydych chi wedi sôn eto am y cynnig o £40 miliwn y flwyddyn gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Ond gadewch inni beidio ag anghofio, neithiwr, fod y Senedd hon wedi gwrthod hynny fel opsiwn, gan fod y Senedd hon yn credu nad oedd hynny'n ddigon i gefnogi ADY ledled Cymru. A nawr, rydym yn gweld Llywodraeth Cymru unwaith eto'n amharod i ddarparu'r dyfarniad cyflog a argymhellir i athrawon. Mae hyn yn ategu'r pwynt eu bod yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu hanwybyddu a'u tanbrisio. Weinidog Cabinet, ni allwn fentro cael streic yn yr hydref oherwydd y sefyllfa hon.

Rwy'n credu bod yr hyn sy'n digwydd ar hyn o bryd yn anfon y neges anghywir at broffesiwn sydd eisoes yn teimlo'r pwysau aruthrol hwnnw. Mae athrawon, fel y disgrifiwyd eisoes gan eich cyd-Aelod o Blaid Cymru, yn ganolog i'n system addysg, ac mae risg wirioneddol y bydd y mater cyffredinol hwn ynghylch cyllid yn effeithio ar recriwtio a chadw athrawon, ac yn y pen draw, ar ganlyniadau i'n plant a'n pobl ifanc.

Rwy'n arbennig o bryderus ynglŷn â'r ffordd y mae arweinwyr ysgolion yn gorfod rheoli'r sefyllfa hon ar hyn o bryd, ac rwy'n datgan buddiant fel llywodraethwr ysgol fy hun. Mae cyrff llywodraethu ysgolion yn gorfod rheoli cyllidebau sydd o dan bwysau, ac os bydd ysgolion yn gorfod pontio'r bwlch ariannu eu hunain, y plant fydd teimlo effaith hynny yn y pen draw. Felly, Weinidog Cabinet, a allwch chi egluro pa sicrwydd y gallwch ei roi i benaethiaid a chyrff llywodraethu na fydd yn rhaid iddynt ddewis rhwng talu eu staff yn deg ac yn briodol a diogelu'r gefnogaeth a'r cyfleoedd sydd ar gael i ddisgyblion?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 3. Cwestiynau Amserol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 3. Topical Questions
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. I think we have rehearsed the reasons why the ALN funding for this year will be difficult in this particular context, but I am committed to working with my colleague the finance Minister on building the sustainable ALN system that we committed to in our manifesto and that I know has support across Wales.

On schools funding more broadly, part of the announcement I made on Monday about the pay award was that we would provide local authorities with additional funding in order that that would not be an additional pressure on school budgets. But we remain committed too to making sure that school leaders and the wider school workforce do feel valued and consulted under this Government, and it is in that spirit that I propose to proceed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Rwy'n credu ein bod wedi trafod y rhesymau pam y bydd cyllid ADY eleni yn anodd yn y cyd-destun penodol hwn, ond rwyf wedi ymrwymo i weithio gyda fy nghyd-Aelod y Gweinidog cyllid ar adeiladu'r system ADY gynaliadwy y gwnaethom ymrwymo iddi yn ein maniffesto ac y gwn fod cefnogaeth iddi ledled Cymru.

Ar gyllid ysgolion yn fwy cyffredinol, rhan o'r cyhoeddiad a wneuthum ddydd Llun ar y dyfarniad cyflog oedd y byddem yn darparu cyllid ychwanegol i awdurdodau lleol fel na fyddai hynny'n bwysau ychwanegol ar gyllidebau ysgolion. Ond rydym yn parhau i fod wedi ymrwymo hefyd i sicrhau bod arweinwyr ysgolion a'r gweithlu ysgolion ehangach yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu gwerthfawrogi a'n bod fel Llywodraeth yn ymgynghori â nhw, ac rwy'n bwriadu parhau yn yr ysbryd hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Datganiadau 90 Eiliad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 4. 90-second Statements
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. I was sad and shocked on the weekend to find out about the passing of the Rt Hon Ann Widdecombe. I'm not going to comment today on the circumstances, but will celebrate the person that she was.

Ann was the MP for Maidstone for 23 years. She served in Government, serving the country that she loved as Minister of State for employment and Minister of State for prisons. Ann became a Member of the European Parliament for South West England in 2019. Her words were that she was there to ensure that the largest democratic vote the United Kingdom has had is fulfilled, and she pushed it through. She became an unlikely national treasure through her appearances on Strictly Come Dancing. She was on Big Brother. She appeared in several pantomimes across the country during the seasons, and even appeared in a production at the Royal Opera House.

She was a dedicated campaigner for animal causes. Ann went against her own party and friends when she was outspoken in supporting the ban on fox hunting, claiming it was immoral not to do so. She stood up for animals like donkeys and their welfare. She fought for the end of the use of animals in circuses. Ann showed us that you could be a true Conservative, a 'small c' conservative, but you can also stand up for your principles, you can go against your party. In tributes, we've heard that Ann was a maverick; she was. She was fearless in debate, she was kind-hearted, she was true to her faith at all times.

I had the pleasure of meeting Ann in 2019. It was a friendship that I cherish more than anything. I walked the streets of Ebbw Vale with her, where I saw women leaving a hair salon and nail bar quickly to have a selfie with the Strictly Come Dancing star that was Ann Widdecombe. She looked perplexed at how she was a star—she just saw herself as Ann. That's the person I knew every time I met her. She's a loss to this country, to our party and to Britain as a whole. We on these benches, and, I hope, across the Chamber, will pay tribute to her family and to the person whom we will long miss. Rest in peace, Ann.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. Cefais fy nhristau a fy synnu dros y penwythnos wrth glywed am farwolaeth y Gwir Anrhydeddus Ann Widdecombe. Nid wyf am wneud sylwadau heddiw ar yr amgylchiadau, ond fe wnaf ei dathlu fel unigolyn.

Roedd Ann yn Aelod Seneddol dros Maidstone am 23 mlynedd. Gwasanaethodd yn Llywodraeth y DU, gan wasanaethu'r wlad yr oedd yn ei charu fel y Gweinidog Gwladol dros gyflogaeth a Gweinidog Gwladol dros garchardai. Daeth Ann yn Aelod o Senedd Ewrop dros Dde-orllewin Lloegr yn 2019. Yn ei geiriau hi, roedd yno i sicrhau bod y bleidlais ddemocrataidd fwyaf y mae'r Deyrnas Unedig wedi'i chael yn cael ei gwireddu, ac fe'i gwthiodd drwodd. Daeth yn drysor cenedlaethol annhebygol drwy ei hymddangosiadau ar Strictly Come Dancing. Bu ar Big Brother. Ymddangosodd mewn sawl pantomeim ledled y wlad yn y tymhorau pantomeim, ac fe ymddangosodd mewn cynhyrchiad yn y Tŷ Opera Brenhinol hyd yn oed.

Roedd yn ymgyrchydd ymroddedig dros achosion anifeiliaid. Aeth Ann yn erbyn ei phlaid ei hun a'i ffrindiau pan oedd yn ddi-flewyn-ar-dafod ei chefnogaeth i'r gwaharddiad ar hela llwynogod, gan honni ei bod yn anfoesol peidio â'i gefnogi. Safodd o blaid anifeiliaid fel asynnod a'u lles. Ymladdodd dros wahardd defnyddio anifeiliaid mewn syrcasau. Dangosodd Ann i ni y gallech fod yn Geidwadwr go iawn, ceidwadwr 'c fach', ond y gallech chi hefyd sefyll dros eich egwyddorion, gallwch fynd yn erbyn eich plaid. Mewn teyrngedau, rydym wedi clywed bod Ann yn rebel; mae'n wir. Roedd yn eofn mewn dadl, roedd ganddi galon garedig, roedd yn driw i'w ffydd bob amser.

Cefais y pleser o gyfarfod ag Ann yn 2019. Roedd yn gyfeillgarwch rwy'n ei drysori'n fwy nag unrhyw beth. Cerddais strydoedd Glynebwy gyda hi, lle gwelais fenywod yn gadael salon trin gwallt a bar ewinedd yn gyflym i gael hunlun gyda seren Strictly Come Dancing, Ann Widdecombe. Ni ddeallai sut roedd hi'n seren—gwelai ei hun yn syml fel Ann. Dyna'r unigolyn roeddwn i'n ei hadnabod bob tro y byddwn yn ei chyfarfod. Mae'n golled i'r wlad hon, i'n plaid ac i Brydain gyfan. Byddwn ni ar y meinciau hyn, ac ar draws y Siambr, gobeithio, yn talu teyrnged i'w theulu ac i'r unigolyn y gwelwn ei cholli'n fawr. Gorffwys mewn hedd, Ann.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 4. Datganiadau 90 Eiliad
